## ![](https://commonwealth-uploads.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/91e03f24-35d3-47c0-ad1e-194e180bb4d9.1647449001747)
## 
## Welcome to Edgeware 
Edgeware is a collectively governed public network and project incubator. 

It is owned, operated and secured by EDG holders who work together to steward the entire economic, organisational and cultural resources of the project through open, meritocratic and democratic processes that are all executed on-chain on the project's own blockchain.

It is the second oldest mainnet chain in the Substrate ecosystem - younger than [Kusama](https://kusama.network), but older than [Polkadot](https://polkadot.network) with over [10M blocks finalised.](https://edgeware.app/#/explorer) 

## No ICO or fundraising event
The project was bootstrapped using a [lockdrop](https://medium.com/commonwealth-labs/whats-in-a-lockdrop-194218a180ca), where holders of ETH could lock their tokens for 3, 6, 9 or 12 months in return for receiving EDG.
It was also possible for smart contracts holding ETH to signal on behalf of their holdings, enabling [Binance](Binance announcement), Coinbase and [Aragon](https://github.com/aragon/AGPs/blob/master/AGPs/AGP-35.md) to receive distributions on behalf of their users.
The total ETH locked in the process finalised at 1,199,728 ETH, with signaled funds (from smart contracts) at 4,346,544 ETH with over 4000 different Edgeware addresses created in the lockdrop process, from over 10,000 transactions.

Binance finally distributed the tokens in March 2022, creating a massive long-tail of EDG holders.
## Wide and fair distribution
With over 90% of the token distributed to the public in the lockdrop, the door was opened to a community of holders who could mediate the decision making powers of the founding team Commonwealth Labs. 

Edgeware was originally positioned as a platform for _incubating governance experiments_, in the end the broad distribution has ensured Edgeware is itself the primary experiment.

title: Edgeware treasury fund, proposal process and timelines
body:
# **Edgeware treasury fund, proposal process and timelines**
## **Introduction**

- As with everything in the community the proposal process and template is a work in progress.


- It is designed to enable newcomers and existing community members to share a common standard.


- The process and template can/will be amended over time in line with experience and feedback.


- It is also expected that we will automate elements to speed up decision making, assure transparency and ensure obligations are met on both sides.


## **What is the Edgeware community fund? **

Edgeware has an on-chain public treasury composed of funds from several sources, including transaction fees, validator fees, and inflation. 

It is one of the very first examples of a _Layer 1 Protocol DAO_ - a digital community with its own economic engine and organisational infrastructure, enabling the funding of creative contributions from a decentralised work-force. 

The blockchain uses the [Substrate SDK](https://substrate.dev) and is part of the emerging Polkadot ecosystem and was fairly launched without a funding event in 2018 as part of the [lockdrop](https://medium.com/commonwealth-labs/whats-in-a-lockdrop-194218a180ca) that gave it one of the [widest and fairest distributions in crypto](https://blog.edgewa.re/the-edgeware-lockdrop-debriefed/).

You can view the current holdings of the Community Fund by opening [Polkadot JS](https://polkadot.js.org/apps) which is an interface that offers live chain data and switching to Edgeware and clicking into the Treasury tab in the Governance drop down.  

Anyone can put forward a proposal to the community and as a result can be used for practically anything that benefits the development, utility and awareness of Edgeware - either directly or indirectly, the argument is yours to make.

title: How to execute a SimpleMajority proposal
body:
**UPDATE 

The below italic was received as feedback to this and clarifies a little the role of Super and Simple Majority votes. 

----

_The super majority bias prevents a small number of participants to enact a change on the current state, which is supposed to he canonical. It is normal and desirable to require a vast majority to change consensus parameters or previously agreed quantities, and only a minority to stop those changes._

_For treasury funding, this is different: with low participation, projects face the risk of being blocked by a minority even though there is no real consensus on the funding state itself by definition._

_----- _

We have agreed to using '[SimpleMajority](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/1563-simplemajority-a-proposed-edgeware-governance-standard)' as an Edgeware governance standard. 

A SimpleMajority proposal is one that only requires a majority - aka over 51% of votes to pass, this ensures we have a bias for approval, without this, the general will of many smaller holders  can be easily overruled by a single party locking 6x against a proposal. 

In general, it is felt that this approach puts the power into the hands of the broader community, rather than individuals.

## **How to execute a SimpleMajority proposal**

The process is currently a little complicated, requiring a number of stages and council approval. Our aim is to automate this via adjustments to the existing treasury pallet. 

In the mean time, here's how you do it.

Head to the [Polkadotjs app](https://polkadot.js.org/apps), switch to Edgeware and click into the [treasury tab ](https://polkadot.js.org/apps/#/treasury)which is located in the governance drop down menu.

title: Edgeware funding proposal master template
body:
# **Edgeware Proposal template**
## **Why use a template?**

You might have a great concept, team and plan but if you can't communicate the key points into clearly defined proposal then all of your hard work will be in vain.

This template outlines the key requirements you should consider when submitting a proposal.

Each numbered section can be used to create a template and give you a checklist to consider.

It's worth noting that every proposal and every team is different - so treat this as a guide, rather than a bureaucratic nightmare.

--------

1. **Date of proposal**
2. If/as the proposal is updated this should be noted
3. Over time we hope to have a form of version control
4. **Author/s of proposal **
5. Name
6. Contact details
7. Telegram / Discord / Element
8. **Proposal summary**
9. TL:DR of key aspects that ensures people have all the key information up top.
10. Paragraph outline
11. Work completed to date
12. Community participation
13. Member/Partner support
14. Funding request
15. **Member/Partner support* **(note this will be a subject of a separate post)
16. Which established community members support this proposal?
17. Are they providing the 5% bonding fees required to propose?
18. Are they also staking (risking) reputation / funds to assure milestones are met?
19. What support are they delivering the proposal?
20. Is this support part of the funding request?
21. What is their relationship to the project and/or team?
22. **Background information**
23. Set the context to the proposal
24. Help us understand where you are coming from
25. **Problem statement**
26. What is the challenge your proposal addresses?
27. **Proposed solution**
28. How does your proposal address the challenge?
29. **Work to date**
30. What stage is the proposal:
31. discussion
32. concept
33. research & development
34. proof of concept
35. emerging project
36. established project
37. **How does the solution work? **
38. Explain things step by step
39. You can use bullet points
4

title: Automatic Votedown - you dont know what you dont know
body:
Dear Edgizens,

I am writing to express my disappointment in the staking upgrade proposal referenda 137. Unfortunately, the proposal lacks any meaningful discussion / information about what it entails or how it would impact Edgeware.

Without this information, it is impossible for us to properly evaluate the proposal and make an informed decision. It is our responsibility as decision-makers to ensure that we are making decisions that are in the best interests of the chain, and this requires that we have all of the necessary information at our disposal.

I strongly believe that it is not in Edgewares best interests to blindly approve proposals without knowing exactly what they entail or having discussion. For this reason, I believe it is appropriate to automatically vote down proposals that lack sufficient information.

I hope that you will consider this perspective and join me in voting down this proposal.

Sincerely,

Bugz

	- Allocation slider for split voting on EdgeApps (post-Gov 2.0)

	- Include community-funded pallets ([SuperSig](https://github.com/kabocha-network/pallet_supersig), [Subscription](https://github.com/kabocha-network/pallet_subscription))

	- Provision for assignments of multiple on-chain reputation tags at once 

## -> **Advance level:** (Tentative) 
	- ParaBridge, a standard based on XCMP-based bridge with Edgeware as a hub (similar to cosmos IBC structure) and evolve it for hybrid deployments (so protocols can leverage the performance of Edgeware and security of any bridged parachain together)

	- [Territories](https://gov.edgewa.re/discussion/4197-edgeware-app-governance-feature-expansion-territories-group-notifications-): on-chain sub-communities/DAOs (leveraging a modified version of SuperSig or Society pallet)
	- Provision for NFT burning as a treasury bond (idea thread on the same coming up by Gagan)


(Fun fact: We discussed the 'allocation slider for split voting' idea in the community calls way before Gov 2.0 but as the split logic is already developed by Parity, the difficulty for the idea changed from an advance to an easier level.)

Original Motivation
===================

Setting up blockchain infrastructure is difficult, time consuming, and expensive:

-   It requires a level of server development expertise that many do not have

-   It's costly to run a full node nearly continuously, especially when your dApp's traffic is low and inconsistent. 

-   Running production level infrastructure is especially tricky. You need to autoscale quickly to handle bursty traffic, and you want to provide services in different regions around the world to provide low latency services - all of this is incredibly costly, but comes with significant economies of scale for a provider.

-   DevOps requires constant attention - time that would be better spent elsewhere building.

A shared node API service helps mitigate these barriers of entry to trying accessing a new protocol by reducing all these costs to near zero. We manage all the nodes for our users and distribute them across the world (with intelligent routing) to achieve global scalability from day 1, we monitor each node and ensure that they meet certain service levels, and we have the expertise and scale to handle production workloads and high peak traffic.

In summary, we try to reduce the pain of getting started on Edgeware Network and minimise the costs of accessing secure nodes while traffic from your dApp is low. title: Talent Pool Framework
body:
{This framework is currently in the draft stage. Parameters are subject to change based on the discussions by the community members/contributors.}

## Summary
	In Edgeware’s journey to becoming a sustainable ecosystem from just a governance experiment, lots of talented enthusiasts joined the efforts as solo contributors or as teams/entities. After the reduced contributions and involvement from the founding team Commonwealth Labs, the initiative called Edgeware Agency (by ex-CW Labs’ member Thom Ivy) became the largest collective looking after the majority of the operations, maintenance and (business/technical) developments for a year. And then the Agency itself got decentralized which accelerated contributors’ onboarding as solo contributors with/without the newly introduced SCU framework to avoid governance bottlenecks. 
	As of today, we have 25+ contributors of different contribution types and diverse backgrounds. The on-chain treasury indirectly the inflation (6.2% currently) has been the backend of the sustainability of the Edgeware ecosystem without any kind of token sales or VC backings. To complement the most recent ‘[Re-rating framework for contributors](https://gov.edgewa.re/discussion/8791-rerating-framework-for-contributors)’ i.e. to increase the sustainability scope even further, this framework aims to explore the possibility of outsourcing the community-judged & proven talent which is cultivated within the Edgeware ecosystem to other web3 projects looking for contributors/employees so the contributors can rely less on the incentives from the on-chain treasury supporting the Edgeware ecosystem in the process.

## Clauses for contributors:
- Need at least one treasury tip/proposal approved by the community.

title: Tokenguard data analytics
body:
Due to the crypto bear market situation we decided at Tokenguard to focus on providing on-chain user related data analytics tool and developing useful features for L1 blockchains and L2 protocols based on Substrate and EVM ecosystems. 

The main goal is to increase protocol revenues, grow user base and understand user flows to make better business decisions.

Web3 creators still don’t have a tool delivering the most important data to them – user data insights. They can’t understand user acquisition/conversion paths and are losing money, because they can’t either measure and increase users' engagement or monitor the efficiency of marketing activities. 

At the same time protocol creators can’t access the data they need, hence they’re either enforced to spend $ to create backend tools for tracking user data or have to use numerous tools to find basic user insights (Subscan, Dune Analytics, Etherscan).

We can propose delivering data analytics tool for Edgeware DAO community, which would consist of the following features:

- no-code and no-SQL dashboard with user data analytics insights 
- user groups analysis over time
- users behavior on-chain (staking, whale wallets analysis, user engagement over time)
- user sources tracking
- transactions analysis over time
- alerting & monitoring 
- RAW data access
- Data Analyst consultations 
- sharing and embedding dashboards on the website
- custom fields and charts


Please find link to exemplary AlephZero testnet demo dashboard [here](http://demo.tokenguard.io/azero-testnet)

We're happy to deliver fully customizable on-chain data analytics tool for Edgeware DAO community based on custom metrics, which you consider as crucial for community growth.

body:
## ![](https://assets.commonwealth.im/05626d16-9243-488a-8ee7-d6b702538383.svg)
## 
## Summary
	Contributors' Support Program allows anyone to support the currently non-treasury-funded contributors to continue their contributions to the Edgeware community through the limited monthly editions of NFTs. This program aims to provide basic minimal monthly incentives for Edgeware contributors who are consistent with their contributions (until the market situation improves).

## The Motto
	The self-sustainability (powered by on-chain treasury) of the Edgeware ecosystem and the contributors are dependent on each other. But because of the ongoing market situation, we entered into a paradox where everyone's approach towards solving the same problem became quite distinct from each other. This resulted in the majority of the contributors not being incentivised at all for 8+ months! Many already gave up while few are still contributing voluntarily. These few contributors came up together to solve the paradox by committing themselves to the more consistent, accountable and transparent contribution structures under the unified non-guaranteed Contributors' Support Program.

## Program Layout
- Basic minimal monthly incentives per contributor: 350 USD (utilising bridged USDT or BUSD on EdgeEVM)
- Total number of NFTs per month = Total number of contributors fulfilling the CSP Clauses
- Each month on the same day, the total number of CSP-eligible contributors will be determined and the new mint contract will be deployed using ThirdWeb. {[https://portal.thirdweb.com/pre-built-contracts/nft-drop](https://portal.thirdweb.com/pre-built-contracts/nft-drop)}
- Once the NFT metadata, mint parameters and recipient multisig details are set, the Admin and Creator permissions of the contract for the deployer address will be permanently removed before hosting the new minting UI on [https://edgeware.io/csp](https://edgeware.io/csp).
- This program will not have any royalties or platform fees.

title: Create legal entities tied to a crypto address using Edgeware
body:
**LexBridge <-> Kali DAO **

Request for Proposal: Seeking an Edgeware/Polkadot developer to complete this project. 
Message @aitheric on Telegram/ [aitheric@protonmail.com](mailto:aitheric@protonmail.com) if you are interested in working on this project. 


**Goal: **
Create legal entities tied to a crypto address using Edgeware

**Background: **
Being able to create a legal entity tied to a crypto address can be useful for new projects or for tax reasons. A 'Series LLC' is a type of LLC that can have hundreds of 'child LLCs'. Each Child LLC can be assigned its own owner. For this project, the 'Child LLC' is assigned an owner based on a crypto address, which is signified both by a legal contract as well as a crypto-token/NFT.

This proposal was originally submitted by Etherize, a LLC/DAO company that was disbanded soon after. Around that time, a very similar project called Kali was released, supporting Ethereum. The goal is now to expand upon Kali's platform to also support Edgeware.

**Requirements:**
Add in support for using Edgeware (Polkadot) to Kali's front end repository.

Legal contract should be generated and signed using the wallet. A token/NFT should be generated upon signing.

**Implementation:**

Fork the Kali front end.
A user should be able to select the Polkadot wallet when using the Kali front end.
If they do so, rather than create an Ethereum DAO, the process should be changed to only create a NFT on Edgeware. The name of the DAO/LLC should be included in the NFT details.

title: Proposal: Establishment of Legal Entity for Edgeverse DAO
body:
This proposal seeks funding for the initial registration expenses of Edgeverse DAO LLC in the Marshall Islands.

As mentioned in [earlier posts](https://gov.edgewa.re/discussion/14795-edgeverse-dao-pioneering-a-subdao-for-enhanced-edgeware-dynamics), we are establishing a multichain DAO to enhance the Edgeware blockchain. We are partnering with MiDAO to register our DAO.

**Introduction**
The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) stands as the foremost jurisdiction for Decentralized Autonomous Organizations (DAOs) and Web3 projects globally.

**Legal Entities**
The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) provides options for both for-profit and non-profit DAO LLCs, as well as Series DAO LLCs. These legal entities are built upon the LLC framework and tailored to accommodate the distinctive requirements of DAOs and Web3 projects.

**Benefits of Legal Entities**
- Limited liability for members of the entity
- Corporate personhood for property ownership, contract signing, opening bank accounts, etc.
- Tax optimization


**Benefits of RMI DAO LLC**
- No trustees, directors, officers, or managers with additional liability or responsibility
- All documents, ownership, and records can be securely stored on the blockchain
- Most members have the option to maintain anonymity
- Governance by smart contracts, permitted by law


**For-profit DAO LLC**
For-profit DAO LLCs are liable to a 3% Gross Revenue Tax (GRT), applicable to all earned income and interest, excluding capital gains and dividends.

**Relationship with the United States**
The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) is an independent nation outside the jurisdiction of the United States. Numerous RMI laws, including corporate laws, draw inspiration from Delaware's legal framework. In the absence of specific statutes or case law within the RMI, its courts may refer to Delaware case law for guidance.

**Digital Asset Regulations**
At present, the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) lacks specific laws or regulation

Now that he has entered the active slots, he has increased the commissions to 100%, and thus, nominators who trusted him when the commission was reasonable are no longer earning any staking rewards. We tried to reach out to him via the dedicated community validator channel assigned to him on the official discord server and he didn't respond in 2 months.

Exploiting validators' details:

ilgio - mWMr2t6Nus1nus5Xmiyq37hieLD99Ff95xuJEuvmbFhRkh5

ilgio/2 - hkFNJdxmXhZ1iNwiaHuH7dsVerYLc3oHNW3DdSjAoke672k

Validators who had 100% commission from the start can be referred to as private validators, and they are not considered exploiters, as nominators wouldn't nominate them in the first place.


Another public validator {not an exploiter} Vismay (DFS), is looking to discontinue his validator, but he lost his keys for the validator stash. Thus, he requested that nominations be removed from his validator through democracy so he could shut down his node to avoid slashing his nominators.

## **Introduction**
I’ve used this proposal and process to trial a new structure for people to run through that is simple, easy to understand and generalisable to all domains. 

It seemed only fair that I use my own proposal to dogfood, what is effectively my own suggestion. 

It aims to standardises timelines, responses and to ensure better communication for **voters** and **proposers** alike.

This approach is, as the overall proposal, a work in progress, so consider this an emerging set of standards, that will only work, if we all agree to try it. 

It starts with a very simple idea - a proposal has 3 clear stages **DRAFT**, **REVIEW** and **FINAL.**

_Voter responsibilities: _

- 1 week of discussion, comment and responses
- Questions and comments should be clear and considerate 
- Keep an open mind and treat this as a collaborative process

- **Version 2: **submit** REVIEW **proposal taking into account DRAFT comments

- REVIEW aims to include responses to questions as Q&

**Diving In: **

**1.MARKET MAKING | WHAT?(in brief)**

	The term market maker refers to a firm or individual who actively quotes two-sided markets in a particular security, providing bids and offers (known as asks) along with the market size of each. Market makers provide liquidity and depth to markets and profit from the difference in the bid-ask spread.

	A market maker participates in the securities market by providing trading services for investors and boosting liquidity in the market. They specifically provide bids and offers for a particular security in addition to its market size.Market makers must also quote the volume in which they're willing to trade along with the frequency of time they will quote at the best bid and best offer prices. Market makers typically profit off of the difference between the bid and ask spread.

	This Market Making activity is a very time and resource intensive task, due to which it has traditionally been done by huge corporations having considerable financial resources and capable personnel at their disposal. This service we currently run for the Edgeware community is available via:

We are requesting **EDG 3,945,370** to pay for the delivery of our services during Q3.

Full details of our proposal can be found via this link:

[https://docs.google.com/document/d/1JKYDfIX91LSAWf-BwaBiPVJU1rSkMI-HAb6jAkTmgKs/edit?usp=sharing](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1JKYDfIX91LSAWf-BwaBiPVJU1rSkMI-HAb6jAkTmgKs/edit?usp=sharing)

---------- Proposal Details Overview -----------

Setting up blockchain infrastructure is difficult, time-consuming, and expensive:

- It requires a level of DevOps skills that many do not have. An Edgeware node, for example, requires knowledge of SSL certificate handling, WebSocket management, HTTPS management, firewall configuration, security measures, monitoring, reporting, upgrades etc.
- It’s incredibly costly to run a node. Since we own and operate our infrastructure our cost structures are fair and more sustainable than cloud providers where one can expect massive increases in price.
- Running production-level infrastructure is not trivial. You need to autoscale quickly to handle sudden increases in traffic which is very common when new projects launch. Our infrastructure uses an intelligent cluster stack whereby sudden increases in traffic are expertly scaled up and down as needed without the need for intervention.
- It requires time. Time is the most valuable resource for projects. Most projects simply do not have the time to spend on DevOps, especially in crunch moments.

title: Edgeware upgrade to substrate 4.
body:
The upcoming upgrade of Edgeware - which is not only a runtime upgrade, otherwise there would be no need for validators to upgrade their node - brings us in line with substrate 4. There are little changes that are specific to Edgeware, but some of those are functional changes that people should keep in mind. Here are the ones I see as very important for everybody to know about. I am trying to be exhaustive, but may extend the list if I think of more later.

1. The confidence voting delay has been corrected back from 1 day to 1 week. It was always supposed to be 1 week, but had been set to 1 day only by mistake since the last releases. It is meant to be long to really allow people with personal conviction to leverage their funds more than others. It affects how long tokens are locked when someone votes with conviction. There is an exponential multiplier that goes from 0 to 32 times the locking period. Votes with no conviction count for only 10% (0.1x) but don't lock tokens, votes with 1x lock with multiplier 1, votes with 2x lock with multiplier 2, votes with 3x lock with multiplier 4, etc. till votes with 6x that lock with multiplier 32. Currently voting 6x is locking the tokens for 32 days. With the release it is going to be 32 WEEKS so please, bear this in mind when voting! Now people with high conviction can really leverage their votes vs others as it will require a much stronger belief to vote with full power. Take care especially of the UI that shows some locking information based on what it sees on chain at a given time. For instance, if you build a transaction just before the upgrade and vote 6x, you may be locked for much longer than expected depending on when the lock expires. So keep this in mind when voting.
2. The staking pallet now handles the case too many nominators (128+) differently than before. The additional ones are put in a queue, but the choice of which is included and which isn't is not purely on stake, but nominators are batched within bags o

title: OnFinality High Performance Public Infrastructure (Q3 2022)
body:
**Proponent:** jH3nezdr2kn7M4jqoqVz27AUcPP99WgB1QgkhL5UJCu8b2d

**Date:** 11th October, 2022

**Requested EDG:** 13,140,086.50

**Short description:** Ongoing costs for the running of high performance, scalable, and reliable public infrastructure for Edgeware Network.


## Original Motivation

Setting up blockchain infrastructure is difficult, time consuming, and expensive:

- It requires a level of server development expertise that many do not have
- It’s costly to run a full node nearly continuously, especially when your dApp’s traffic is low and inconsistent. 
- Running production level infrastructure is especially tricky. You need to autoscale quickly to handle bursty traffic, and you want to provide services in different regions around the world to provide low latency services - all of this is incredibly costly, but comes with significant economies of scale for a provider.
- DevOps requires constant attention - time that would be better spent elsewhere building.

A shared node API service helps mitigate these barriers of entry to trying accessing a new protocol by reducing all these costs to near zero. We manage all the nodes for our users and distribute them across the world (with intelligent routing) to achieve global scalability from day 1, we monitor each node and ensure that they meet certain service levels, and we have the expertise and scale to handle production workloads and high peak traffic.

In summary, we try to reduce the pain of getting started on Edgeware Network and minimise the costs of accessing secure nodes while traffic from your dApp is low. When you grow, you can continue to use our shared API service, or we also [provide access to one click deploy dedicated Edgeware nodes](https://onfinality.io/dedicated_nodes) to any cloud of your choosing.

title: Multi-Sig Overview/FAQ
body:
Multi-Sig Overview/FAQ


What is a Multi-Sig


A Multi-Signature account is Keyless Account. Where a single Edgeware account key and it’s signatory for transactions are _determined*_ by multiple citizens. The participants (accounts) would be responsible for signing transactions to complete the transfer of funds and other on-chain actions. (ie. declaration of a chain Identity) 


The Multi-Signature account transactions are secured via the set participation**_ _threshold.** This is  the required amount of approvers for transactions.

[*This type of account is categorized as **deterministic.**]

title: Treasury Tip: Voluntary Contribution of Edgeware docker builds by Eliott Teiss
body:
This is an appreciation post for the voluntary contribution by [Eliott Teiss](https://twitter.com/EliottTeiss). They have contributed in the form of daily docker builds of the Edgeware node. 
They have employed a code script which collects information related to any updates from Github and creates a new docker image of the same. Further, this docker image can be used by validators, RPC infrastructure providers, exchanges, wallets, explorers and EdgeEVM/EdgeWASM protocols to set up their nodes. These daily builds have been there for over 2 years now.
Recently, they switched their source repository from the [Commonwealth Edgeware Node to the Edgeware Network Edgeware Node](https://github.com/ETeissonniere/substrate-nodeops/commit/6c37d0c07cb9882085472fe3c76629cc4b746727) repository, which means they were building images for Edgeware v3.3.6, but now after the change in the source repository, they are compiling images for Edgeware v4.0.2. In addition to this, we are expected to have docker builds for all the new Edgeware version releases hereafter.
Based on the above information, we can understand that this is a very useful technical domain contribution and will be helpful to the Edgeverse community members wanting to set-up their nodes. Thus, proposing a treasury tip as an appreciation for this contribution.

**You can find the docker build here**: [https://hub.docker.com/r/eteissonniere/edgeware](https://hub.docker.com/r/eteissonniere/edgeware)

## **Summary**
_Root_ is a [Substrate](https://substrate.dev) based governance lab that aims to drive participation in on-chain governance by rethinking the design from the ground up, making proposal collaboration fun, participatory and ultimately more human,

The project tackles the current adversarial relationship between proposers and voters by turning them into meaningful participants, co-creators, organisers and owners of on-chain projects.

Root is built around a collective creation and decision making system that uses a composable voting system inspired by[ Borda’s Count](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borda_count) to compute voting and allow contributors to create _preferendums_ directly linked to the governance pallets.

## **Background**

> _When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to become a good measure - Godhardt's Law_

When addressing the current issues with on-chain governance, we need to begin by focusing on the **fundamental outcome** we have in mind when designing new tools and processes.

We should be very clear as to what certain developments aim to **optimise**, for **who** and what **purpose**, since these problems are all part of a bigger picture.

Without aligning on a core motivation we are in danger of collectively making the overall system worse in aggregate.

A starting point for this north star is _sourcing, sustaining and scaling collective network intelligence._

title: Voting Principles / Perspective
body:
Voting Principles / Perspective

Hello Edgeware Citizens,
	 In anticipation in our future growth I’m providing my **5** voting principles. This is in effort to streamline my cooperation for Edgeware contributors creating funding proposals. The following is a breakdown of the factors towards my voting decision.

The Factors are:

1. **Citizen Reputation/ On Chain Judgment **
2. **Existing Contribution **
3. **Prior Proposal - Project Fulfillment**
4. **Milestone, Deliverables, Timelines  **
5. **Risk to Edgeware**


## _**Bridging of principles: **_

1. I cannot be in support of proposals from a citizen that has a bad judgment from a Registrar. 
2. I can only be in support of good faith agreement for citizen proposals with a prior contribution. 
3. I cannot support an additional proposal if the citizen has outstanding proposals. 

                   (Outstanding proposals are _Project Length > 365 days)_
      4.    I cannot support proposals without clear deliverables and fulfilment deadline/timelines for    those commitments.
      5.     I will not support proposals that I believe could subject or encourage Edgeware to experience unnecessary legal scrutiny or impede our long term sustainability.  

## _**Curiosity:**_

1. This is would be in conflict with the value of our on-chain Identity function and the contributor(s) providing this service. 
2. Good Faith Agreements for initial funding are built on prior contribution. Faith is equal to the display of good faith contribution for Edgeware’s citizens.   
3. I will consider citizens with outstanding proposals (Project Length since incentives > 365 days) with an overwhelming workload.  I will not place additional expectations on a contributor with existing chain fulfillments.

title: [Opinion] Proposal for Bond modifications
body:
**Goal: ** Alleviate any tension for proposers and to promote our democracy by supporting decentralized voting.

          My position is not that proposals have a default democracy approval. My position is that proposals have a default attempt. I would like proposers to be able to submit their Ideas, rate and value to Edgeware in the format they prefer. I want to support our citizen’s right to an open democracy . 

          The Right for Edgeware citizens to vote to express they’re favor in support or against a proposal is provided upon citizenship.

          It is a choice of the proposer to garner support from other Edgeware citizens.


** TLDR**

1. Remove Bond Risk for unpassed proposals
2. Increase Bond to 10%


“_**Problem**”_ The current Bond Risk:

       Alot of time is spent when presenting proposals. Often discourse is regarding a proposal’s structure, value, cost, and impact. Am unsure if this process is sustainable at scale. Primarily due to the time availability of our citizens.  Also unsure if it’s necessary in a decentralized environment and because our Blockchain has had an onchain democracy since it’s LockDrop. 


Reason for Removal and increased bond percentage as the “_**Solution**_”:

       Removing the bond for unsuccessful proposals will remove the tension for unsuccessful attempts in democracy. 

Increase bond by** 5% **to **10%**
         To help counter the risk previous risk of spam. 

         Previously, this counter was supported by the 5% bond risk of unpassed proposals through democracy. This is also to encourage investment into Edgeware. This will effectively ask each proposer to invest at least 10% of what they’re requesting from Edgeware.




Always open for feedback. Intending to send to democracy 1/13/2023 
Sooner, only prompted by the Edgeware community.

title: Re-rating framework for contributors
body:
{This framework is currently in the draft stage. Parameters are subject to change based on the discussions by the community members/contributors.}

## **Purpose of the framework: **
To do treasury management/planning for the longevity of Edgeware’s self-sustainability in bearish market sentiment.

## Calculations:
Framework timeline {FT}: 3 years = 36 months
Current Treasury balance {CTB}: 412.6547 Million EDG
Pending incentives {PI}: SCU’s November Proposal + non-SCU contributor’s incentives until November + OnFinality’s Q4 proposal + Dwellir’s Q4 proposal = ~135 M EDG (included buffer)

Treasury spending available per month (without considering the treasury minting due to inflation) {T1 = (CTB - PI) / FT}: 7.71263056 M EDG

Ideal staking ratio {ISR}: 50%
Current % of total supply staked {TSS}: 21.3%
Current Inflation {CI}: 5.7%
Current Total Supply {CTS}: 7.2703 Billion EDG = 7270.3 Million EDG

Treasury spending available per month (considering the treasury minting due to inflation) 
{T2 = T1+((ISR-TSS)*CI*CTS/(ISR*100*12))}: 27.5351036 M EDG

Infrastructural costs {IC}: JelliedOwl + Bharthcoorg + OnFinality + Dwellir + Subscan

Treasury spending available per month deducting infrastructure costs {T}: T2 - IC

Base incentives {B}: 300 USD equivalent in EDG (with reference price equal to whichever is the highest amongst 0.0004 USD per EDG or the 30-day trailing median price)

Number of solo/team contributors: N

Previous incentives per month of an individual contributor: P
Sum of all the previous incentives per month of individual contributors: S

**Effective incentives for the contributors:** B + [ (T - (B * N)) * P / S ]

- Contributors can deduct their incentives further (than their corresponding effective incentives) if they want.

title: OnFinality High Performance Public Infrastructure (Q2 2022)
body:
[Created as a proposal here](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/treasuryproposal/84-onfinality-high-performance-public-infrastructure-q2-2022)

**Proponent:** jH3nezdr2kn7M4jqoqVz27AUcPP99WgB1QgkhL5UJCu8b2d

**Date:** 7th July, 2022

**Requested EDG:** 1,739,953.45

**Short description:** Ongoing costs for the running of high performance, scalable, and reliable public infrastructure for Edgeware Network.


## Original Motivation

Setting up blockchain infrastructure is difficult, time consuming, and expensive:

- It requires a level of server development expertise that many do not have
- It’s costly to run a full node nearly continuously, especially when your dApp’s traffic is low and inconsistent. 
- Running production level infrastructure is especially tricky. You need to autoscale quickly to handle bursty traffic, and you want to provide services in different regions around the world to provide low latency services - all of this is incredibly costly, but comes with significant economies of scale for a provider.
- DevOps requires constant attention - time that would be better spent elsewhere building.

A shared node API service helps mitigate these barriers of entry to trying accessing a new protocol by reducing all these costs to near zero. We manage all the nodes for our users and distribute them across the world (with intelligent routing) to achieve global scalability from day 1, we monitor each node and ensure that they meet certain service levels, and we have the expertise and scale to handle production workloads and high peak traffic.

In summary, we try to reduce the pain of getting started on Edgeware Network and minimise the costs of accessing secure nodes while traffic from your dApp is low. When you grow, you can continue to use our shared API service, or we also [provide access to one click deploy dedicated Edgeware nodes](https://onfinality.io/dedicated_nodes) to any cloud of your choosing.

title: Exchange B update (Decent Partners assessment)
body:
Hi all, 

A few months back Decent Partners were asked if we would consider helping with the [Exchange B listing](https://gov.edgewa.re/discussion/3862-proposal-market-makerfaciliatated-liquidation-and-exchange-b-final-items), which has been slow, difficult and complex for all involved. 

The original agreement to deliver the listing was taken up by Commonwealth Labs as the responsible party. 

When Commonwealth Labs left, the project was taken up by the Edgeware Agency under the management of Thom Ivy, however for a number of reasons this has stalled - the major issue is around the US regulatory situation.

Upon receiving the listing agreements we reviewed with our UK lawyers and assessed the issues.

The primary issue is that these documents were originally to be signed by Commonwealth Labs as the 'issuer' of EDG. 

Owing to standardised legal agreements, any organisation wishing to engage with a centralised exchange takes on the responsibility of 'the issuer'. 

What this would mean in practice is that were Decent Partners, or any other organisation outside of the US to take on the listing of EDG, then it also takes on the legal liability of being the 'issuer' of EDG.

From our lawyers:
 
> My first more general observation is that under the agreement you would be the issuer. Being an issuer comes with very different and significantly greater risks compared to simply advising on an issuance. My second more specific observation is that, assuming you are doing this in the UK in the name of your UK registered entity, you would likely be considered to be acting as a cryptoasset exchange provider. It is a criminal offence to act as such in the UK without being registered with the UK FCA.

## **Assessment**

The listing process cannot be fulfilled by the Edgeware Agency due to legal restrictions on US corporations, and nor would we recommend that it is done by this entity, since all liability will then pass to this organisation, and away from Commonwealth Labs.

![](https://commonwealth-uploads.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/59b3dc00-aab4-42d4-ac65-e52480b543a0.1658607170632)

# Kabocha Seeds - Outlining the evolving concept for sovereign identity in the EDGVerse and beyond

_Note: the following is a work in progress, everything we are doing is emerging organically. Please ask questions, poke at holes, tell me what is dumb and present your own ideas..._

Kabocha 'Seeds' was one of the central narrative themes in the lead up to and during the successful crowdloan, but so far we have only shared a little bit of information about them. That isn't because we had some sort of incredible masterplan we were slowly drip feeding , but simply because the concept was emerging organically.

From the start, Kabocha has evolved as a response to the challenges we faced and are facing in Edgeware - it is the result of the day to day experience of governing, coordinating and advancing a decentralised network of contributors. 

Currently Edgeware's citizens primarily rely on 'identity' as provided by an EDG address linked to a Commonwealth account - [here is mine](https://gov.edgewa.re/account/jXC7ghviUzVcVySg3eD8prB7C9m6VzK6cw2MTyMTDTUye5q/). 

Rather than developing an 'identity protocol' and then onboarding 'identities', Edgeware is going about things the other way around. We are creating trusted relationships, and building credibility through good old fashioned contribution - it is a meritocracy in the classical sense.

However I don't own that identity. My 'ID' sits on a Commonwealth Labs server.

What is more, I don't have any way to backup any of those posts, or comments, or all the backlinks should the forum disappear - and if it did, there would be no fingerprint on the Edgeware blockchain as a testament to the information having ever existed.

title: Proposal of an Alternate Approach for KAB Distribution
body:
## Proposal of an Alternate Approach for KAB Distribution

In reference to: [https://gov.edgewa.re/discussion/6007-kabocha-genesis-issuance-treasury-and-edg-and-crowdloan-distributions](https://gov.edgewa.re/discussion/6007-kabocha-genesis-issuance-treasury-and-edg-and-crowdloan-distributions)

**Brief:**

This mechanism was discussed in the Community Financial Call of 19th July’22.

This approach will be as follows: 
Instead of the proposed KAB treasury of 6,437,924.018517766 (~ 9.32% of the total KAB supply), the treasury will be around ~5.1% of the total KAB supply(4.9% = crowd-loan rewards + 0.2% = contingency buffer)

**Reason:**

Now that Kabocha is equipped with the Pallet Mint functionality, there is no concrete need(open for discussion) to have a treasury. So instead the remaining amount i.e. the ~4.22% (9.32% - 5.1%) will be distributed to the EDG holders, which will make it ~94.9% of the total KAB supply for the EDG holders effectively.

This will result in two major benefits: 

(a) EDG holders get slightly higher than 1:1 network share in the KAB ecosystem 

(b) KAB will be inflationary in nature, as new tokens will be minted for new proposals, so it makes sense to incentivize the holders by rewarding them with higher network shares during initial distribution.

(c) The rewards for crowd-loan participants remain the same as promised before. 

For this mechanism, the 1.5% founder's rewards as well as the Edgeware recoup can be done using the Pallet Mint functionality, instead of keeping it as a part of the initial treasury.

**Effective Distribution**:

94.9% - EDG holders
5.1% - Treasury- {4.9%(crowd-loan reward)+0.2%(contingency buffer)}
Total - 100%

Others - Minted Using Pallet Mint via democracy after genesis allocation

title: Monthly Incentives' Standards
body:
## Ethos: 
As we enter more and more into the bear market, non-contributing EDG holders will have fewer psychological incentives to hold/stake which could affect the sustainability of the ecosystem in the longer run. While the contributors are not exposed to the same level of financial risks. This could potentially lead to Edgeware becoming a playground for premium bounty hunters. In the current scenario, contributors can claim that they want to invoice with reference to EDG only when the EDG price has increased recently and then switch back to any fiat denomination when the EDG price impacts negatively. We need to set ethical standards to utilize our on-chain treasury so that contributors/ holders who are here for the long term will somewhat be equally benefited.


## Solution: 
Introducing standard clauses and max caps for contributors, setting common grounds for all the periodic contributors. 

**General Clauses**

- Calculate the EDG incentives in USD only. (Setting up one reference for everyone irrespective of your native currency is very crucial in the time of a potential recession. In recent examples, GBP and EUR are getting declined w.r.t. USD slightly/ significantly.)


- Postpaid-only funding. (Periodic contributors usually don’t have significant initial funding requirements. Even if they do have, they can propose the first proposal as prepaid and then switch to postpaid. This indirectly also aligns with ‘underpromise and overdeliver’. )


- [Use of 30-day trailing median](https://replit.com/@ShankarWarang1/30-Days-Trailing-Median-dollarEDG?v=1) instead of 7-day trailing average. (Contributors might try to time the market and propose their proposals accordingly. This can be avoided if we use the 30-day trailing median instead of the previously adopted standard of the 7-day trailing average.)



**Proposed Max Caps for monthly incentives structure**

1. 9000 USD per month for full-time core contributors who have these incentives as the only income source.

title: Public RPC and bootnodes - JelliedOwl
body:
I have had a few expressions of interest in my providing bootnodes and RPC servers for Edgeware, so I'd like to describe what I think I can offer and see if there's more general interest before I spend too much time on it.  I'm happy to provide the service or for someone else to do so - but I think it is potentially needed.

## Proposed infrastructure

I'm proposing to run the following:
- 5 geographically distributed public RPC nodes (providing both substrate native websocket and EVM RPCs)
- Those nodes would also be full archive bootnodes, which can be added to the chainspec - they will have fixed DNS addresses so new nodes can find them.
- The RPCs would be behind a load balancer, so there's a single DNS address for them all (the bootnode part can't be load balanced).

I will aim to provide monthly performance stats when I can - this might not be immediately.

## Potential variations

There are some unknowns in this for me, so the above is the minimum I think I will need.  If I find that I need to separate the RPC and bootnodes, I will - they will all remain full archive nodes.  I won't be increasing the invoice to cover these extra nodes, unless there's desire for me to provide a completely different service.  If I find that I can't provide the services without an excessive number of nodes, I might end up giving a full refund instead - but I don't expect that to happen.

In practice, I will probably run at least 6 nodes to cover outages.

## Load balancing options

The load balancer is my biggest unknown.  I am intending to implement a geographically-aware load balancer (potentially using Cloudflare), which would direct traffic to the nearest node.  I think this is feasible at a reasonable cost, but I might find a showstopper - it's not clear to me that Cloudflare works well with websockets, for example.  If I can't make this work - I might have to fall back to something like a round-robin load balancer.

# Decent Partners Network Services: Project status report August 2022

## Summary

This status report seeks to update the community with the status of all curated projects, their status, their challenges and path to completion.

## What are Network Services (NS), Network Service Fees (NSF), and Network Service Providers? (NSP)

Decent Partners introduced the Network Services concept to Edgeware around 7 months ago - read more [here](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/discussion/3650-decent-partners-an-introduction-to-network-services). 

Network Services sought to address a major bottleneck in the project by creating a clear structure to bridge the existing community with its emerging culture governance structures, onchain processes and the sourcing, development and stewarding of new or emerging contributors. 

In this model, the curator would receive 10% of the proposal on top of the team's budget as a fee paid by the network. 

This 10% covers the risk/reward of a Network Service Provider putting up a 5% bond and developing and managing a proposal to approval and a successful delivery.

In some ways it is an approach analogous to Kusama's 'curator' bounties, except it does not use the bounty pallet and instead focuses more on the off-chain elements of curation. 

Its development has aligned with proposed funding for ongoing network research and development that provides insights and strategies for new waves of projects.

_Pallet Version Control Docs enables the sequential hashing and timestamping of arbitrary data from a governance or publishing platform into the blocks of a Substrate based blockchain, creating foundational assurances that can form the basis for securing higher layer information structures._

## **Background**
In principle DAOs exist to enable a digital collective to coordinate, contribute and make decisions upon creative initiatives in a decentralised manner. The central thesis being that over time they will assemble a greater collective intelligence than is possible in today’s existing organisational structures.

If the promise is to be realised, then trust in the provenance of underlying data structures is paramount, since higher order implementations will only be as credible as the sources on which they depend. 

Existing organisational frameworks for these collectives focus primarily on reading on-chain data and providing a more intuitive interface for members to discuss, debate and move forward together. 

Version controlled documents are a base expectation in most group collaboration scenarios: high-school projects, software development, academia and newsrooms and are fundamental to establishing and iterating human consensus.

title: Edgeware knowledgebase with Peeranha
body:
**Problem**
**Blockchain technology is developing extremely fast. New approaches, blockchains, frameworks, tools and applications appear in the space every day. Effective knowledge sharing is highly important for the crypto community and overall space development. However, the current approach for knowledge sharing in Web3 is proven to be very inefficient.**

**Messengers such as Discord, Telegram, and Slack are the most widely used tools for community knowledge sharing. There are several significant disadvantages of using these tools for community knowledge sharing, particularly Q&A:**
- **Questions have a short window of visibility to the community and disappear in the flow of the new messages in communication threads; **
- **Existing questions are hard to find causing the same questions to be asked repeatedly;**
- **Questions and answers are not indexed by SE engines as Google;**
- **Questions and answers are not curated;**
- **Communities in different messengers and different languages exist in silos.**


**There are asynchronous Q&A tools such as Stack Exchange (Stack Overflow) and Discourse. However, for various reasons these tools are being underutilized. We see several reasons for that.**

**Stack Exchange:**

- **High barrier to entry for the communities. Only the biggest communities have the capacity to start their community on Stack Exchange;**
- **By the time the Stack Exchange community is started, the community is already large enough and used to communicate in Discord, Telegram, or Slack;**
- **There is a chance that Stack Exchange will not allow crypto communities at all.**


**Discourse:**
- **Lack of incentives for users (e.g. such as reputation on Stack Exchange);**
- **Communities are used to communicate in Discord, Telegram, or Slack.**


**There are also philosophical issues with Stack Exchange and Discord where a centralized entity owns collective knowledge of the decentralized communities.**

title: Less WenWenWen, more WhyWhyWhy - an Edgeware community development strategy
body:
![](https://commonwealth-uploads.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/c17e5d80-7f7b-45a2-bd24-b7eed5137bb6.1662623896484)

> The parable of the Blind Men and an Elephant is a story of a group of blind men who have never come across an elephant before and who learn and conceptualize what the elephant is like by touching it. Each blind man feels a different part of the elephant's body, but only one part, such as the side or the tusk. They then describe the elephant based on their limited experience and their descriptions of the elephant are different from each other. In some versions, they come to suspect that the other person is dishonest and they come to blows… 
> [Decred - Forks in the Road](https://github.com/monsieurbulb/forksintheroad/blob/master/Decred_forks_in_the_road.md)

## Diversity is Edgeware's super power and greatest weakness.

Edgeware is a blockchain based internet organisation made up of many strangers contributing across many platforms in many different ways.

We speak _different languages_, come from _different cultures_ and bring _different perspectives_.

We create in _different forms_, we understand ideas through _different lenses_ and we prefer _different communication mediums and styles_ to make our points.

Some like _writing_, others do their talking with _code_, some prefer to tell their story via _imagery_, others speak their truth in _logos and symbols, _others find _talking_ the best way to illuminate their creativity. 

Some of us contribute under _our own names_, some _anonymously_, some _a mix of both_, some maybe even under_ a few aliases_ and others under _team or collective names_.

We utilise governance forums maintained and designed by _outside teams_, a user experience designed by those who don't _understand our specific challenges, _in a system where our _data and credentials are locked in. _

title: Decentralizing Edgeware with Chain Leads
body:
As we head into 2020, I wanted to drop this post as a "decentralization roadmap" for Edgeware to accompany [@drewstone](/edgeware/account/hwR8hAatmmdupBLXQSxLUPBa8GhRomLD9hf6iRtFeXs8fcY)'s [Proposed Technical Roadmap](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/878-edgeware-builders-guild-2021-technical-roadmap-ideas). From a token distribution perspective, Edgeware is quite decentralized already. However, this isn’t yet reflected in the network’s core contributors. 

## [Link to the full proposal (with estimated budget, open for comments)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1U5KsZWBrUBZ006J1Rwx4wX8uWLqT4xS8tBDNS2SJBB0/edit?usp=sharing)

We’d like to propose forming a new team of chain-leads, who would then set up BD and developer incentives, to take this step towards the original goal of an on-chain treasury that self-perpetuates the chain.

This would be conducted in an open process, where potential chain leads would post their proposals, and community members would debate them before the proposal goes to a vote. Hopefully, this would resolve any questions around how existing leadership positions are compensated, as [@mrbulb](/edgeware/account/jXC7ghviUzVcVySg3eD8prB7C9m6VzK6cw2MTyMTDTUye5q) has [mentioned](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/861-bwg-now-edg-agency-update-payments). 

Individuals from Commonwealth Labs that want chain-leadership positions would go through this open process, like any other candidate. After all, while Commonwealth Labs helped launch Edgeware, there may be individuals or organizations that may be better suited to driving the project forward. This would also replace any block grants requested by Commonwealth. 

**Chain-leads **would be**:**
- Directly accountable to Edgeware governance. Their compensation and performance would be individually approved by the chain, and paid out from the treasury.
- Paid industry-standard compensation. For a team of 5-6 chain leads, a ballpark figure is ~$500k or 6 * ~$80k, wh

title: Integration with Subsocial
body:
Hey, Edgeware community,

I'm Alex - the founder of [Subsocial.Network](https://Subsocial.Network).
I would like to discuss possible features, that would integrate Edgeware into Subsocial.

## What is Subsocial?
- It is an open protocol for decentralized censorship-resistant social networking on Substrate & IPFS.
- We have a running betanet (1.9m blocks so far) and a web app integrated with the betanet and Polkadot.js Extension.
- Subsocial is supported by Web3 Foundation via grants program, and we are part of Substrate Builders Program by Parity.

## Current features of Subsocial:
- Create a profile for a blockchain account.
- Create a space (similar to a blog or group on other social networks).
- Post in a space.
- Comment on a post, reply to a comment.
- Edit space, post, comment, profile.
- Upvote/downvote a post, a comment.
- Follow a space.
- Follow an account.
- Create different roles and permissions for your space(s) to control who can do what kind of actions (extrinsics) in your space(s), e.g. create Moderator, Editor, Member roles and assign them to the accounts that need these roles. 
- See a personalized feed of new posts from the spaces you follow.
- See notifications about activities related to your account: e.g. somebody followed your space or account, replied to your post or comment, reacted to your post or comment, etc.
- Full-text search over profiles, spaces, posts.
- SEO - search engine optimization - all pages of Subsocial are indexed by Google: profiles, spaces, posts, comments. You can check it with the next Google Search query: https://www.google.com/search?q=site%3Aapp.subsocial.network
- All text and images are stored in IPFS.

title: Proposal: Calibrating the Edgeware treasury budget
body:
We currently have a treasury of 550m EDG worth around ~$4 million USD. All of this has been printed in the 10 months since mainnet launch.

The amount printed remains constant unless adjusted by governance. This means we're on track to print another ~$5m/year from Feb 2021-Feb 2022.

- **We aren't able to deploy $5m/year effectively** towards builders, PR/community, exchanges/market development, and all the other functions related to running the chain.
- **Having a large treasury is a vector for attack. **We already have a large treasury surplus.
- **Treating EDG as something which can be arbitrarily printed out of thin air reduces confidence in the value of EDG. **I don't even think we can sell that much EDG per year.


Speaking as a stakeholder in the network, I would prefer if treasury inflation were either 1) reduced on a regular schedule, or 2) reduced once and then carefully supervised by on-chain governance.

---

## **How much treasury EDG can we effectively deploy?**

I am working off the [budget proposed by Dillon last week](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1U5KsZWBrUBZ006J1Rwx4wX8uWLqT4xS8tBDNS2SJBB0/edit#heading=h.cvbp7r2i0r32) in his Chain Leads post. It allocates 525m EDG for a year of operations:

- $525k/year to chain leads
- $700k/year to builders
- $525k/year to marketing, PR, brand, and community
- $525k/year to market development, e.g. exchanges (but this may not be an expense after Feb-Mar 2021 once key deals are done)
- $350k/year to ecosystem incentives
- $350k/year to BuilDAO (but by my estimates, it would be premature to re-up till early 2022)
- $700k/year to parachain bonding


I think we should try to follow this budget, but it will take time to ramp up to deploying this much EDG effectively, and we will not actually spend that much.

Chain leads will take time to onboard. Projects will take time to spin up. BuilDAO and some other expenses have already been funded.

We should fund high-caliber chain leads and projects, and be comfortable

title: UMA derivatives on Edgeware
body:
A quick update on my forays in the UMA-verse. I've finished the DeFi-Academy course. It outlines a minimal implementation of a derivatives platform using Remix and Solidity. The contracts are not production-ready, but it teaches the basic UMA architecture.

I don't think it's useful at this point to fork UMA on Edgeware or rewrite the code in Rust. In my opinion it is smart to dock on to this existing and well-advanced protocol with its clever priceless design. In case of a price request a smart contract call can be bridged to the UMA Data Verification Mechanism on Ethereum. There is no need for a fast execution of this call, the bridge wouldn't form any hindrance thus. Price requests ask UMA token holders to vote on the value of a price identifier at a historic timestamp. This process takes 2-4 days where said holders commit and reveal their votes on-chain. 

All synthetics are backed by collateral, ideally by DOT, KSM and EDG. Seeing that D-trade will first use a couple of ERC20 tokens as collateral, the preferred ones are not possible to use yet. I don't have an overview of which of the UMA contracts need to be redeployed on Edgeware.

This morning I had a meeting with Edson Alcala from UMA, who created the course. He is working on an UMA Plugin for Remix. My feedback was that he should focus on making it as easy as possible to launch production ready synthetics that integrate with UMA. He too had thought about deploying on another chain and that we could do this together!

body:

title: Edgeware Assets Pallet Update
body:
Over the last month or so, I've been working on adding some new features to Substrate's asset pallet. Though the PR is taking too long to merge into substrate, I am instead cloning it directly into Edgeware, as a pallet which we will maintain and add necessary features to. The functionality that differs from Substrate's asset implementation is the ability to allow other modules in our runtime to:
- Create and interact with assets
- Mint assets
- Freeze assets
- Burn assets


The PR can be found here: https://github.com/hicommonwealth/edgeware-node/pull/276

Where is this useful?
- We want a bridge between EVM and native assets. This bridge could manage, as the "owner", a bunch of different assets (namely EVM assets) and allow minting those assets into the native assets system.
- I am building pallets for my own applications that I want to own native assets, being able to mint/burn/freeze assets.
- Future pallets would be able to be built to interact with assets (potentially Treasury reward when we find new use cases)
- For any future bridges that are created trusted/trustless, the developers can utilise this asset functionality: for example for renVM pallet or chainbridge pallet or trustless bridge pallets.


Where is the room for discussion?
- I think this is a good kick-off for the Edgeware EVM <-> Edgeware Native Assets wrapper bridge, where we can provide a way to mint/freeze/burn ERC20 assets from native substrate assets and vice versa.
- Our assets pallet will support all mining/freezing/burning functionality by default. If we want specific tokens to have a subset of this functionality then it needs to be tracked by the bridge itself.
- How should ownership be handled? If the bridge takes ownership of assets being crated _**FROM**_ Edgeware EVM assets, what are the consequences?

title: Hedgeware, a canary network and parachain.
body:
_Disclaimer: This is an idea I had and am writing for the sake of sharing ideas. It is in no way binding or entirely reflective of what I plan to be building in the coming year. My focus is on seeing the next Edgeware upgrade to fruition and putting more effort into parachain work, sparking ideas and interest and work for newcomers._

One of the most common questions we receive time and time again is whether Edgeware will be a parachain. The short answer is yes; the long answer can maybe be described in this proposal. As this is a proposal this is not binding, but merely some ideas and suggestions for a future path to parachain pride.

This chain is to be called Hedgeware, as a hedge against the difficulties of swapping consensus of the current Edgeware for Polkadot consensus. Little is known or spoken about this process from Parity and so new action is potentially called for. Most "parachains" in the ecosystem aren't even live chains and will likely never need to deal with the qualms of swapping consensus.

**The basics of this proposal are as follows:**
- Create and launch Hedgeware as a parachain from day 1.
- Continue to work on and fund swappable consensus work.

**Why?**
- A canary network has been mentioned before, this serves as that.
- Swapping consensus for Edgeware validators could be a messy process and lead to consensus failures on Edgeware.
- Edgeware wants to be a parachain in one form or another.

title: Edgeware Ecology - a framework for understanding the ecosystem
body:
**Intro**
Since blockchains are social systems, the mechanism design underlying the social coordination, incentivisation and management of individuals and collectives is perhaps the single most important barrier to Edgeware’s ecosystem development. 

**Challenge**
There are many different roles, responsibilities, interests and agendas within the project and defining the names, language, reward mechanics, social status, reputation accrual, accountability and roadmaps is imperative if the project is to have any chance at achieving anything close to social scalability. 

**About this document**
The linked document is a work in progress document that attempts to create a simple framework for understanding the different components of the emerging ecosystem through a structure that provides more context than is currently available.

The aim is that it can provide a consistent framework to enable Edgeware to socially scale its collective endeavours, whilst also retaining a flexible and nuanced approach to how different individuals and groups can contribute to the chain.

As noted - this is a working document, so all input / comment is appreciated. 

It is one part of an larger Community Roadmap which will be published soon, that seeks to outline the key opportunities and. challenges facing the network alongside recommendations for the next 12 months activities that will also include a series of already published and soon to be published project proposals.

title: Tontine - a defi lottery idea
body:
So this has had about 5 minutes thought but I was inspired by a scene I saw in 'Les Miserables' - recent film, not the musical. 

In it, women are collecting  and managing money in a 'Tontine' - they throw money in  together and it goes towards big events - funerals, weddings, a big moment where one cannot afford alone.

From Wikipedia: 

> A **tontine** ([/ˈtɒntaɪn, -iːn, ˌtɒnˈtiːn/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English)) is an investment plan for raising capital, devised in the 17th century and relatively widespread in the 18th and 19th centuries.
> It enables subscribers to share the risk of living a long life by combining features of a group [annuity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annuity_(financial_contracts)) with a kind of mortality [lottery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lottery). 
> Each subscriber pays an agreed sum into the fund and thereafter receives a periodical payout. 
> As members die, their payout entitlements devolve to the other participants, and so the value of each continuing payout increases. 
> On the death of the last member, the scheme is wound up.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tontine#cite_note-1)

Seemed to contain some interesting ideas that could have a crypto spin - namely collective funding (aka a DAO), a lottery (albeit a mortality one) which might touch on the long term value of crypto... 

Haven't yet thought how this kind of an idea might relate to the ideas around making Edgeware the best place to work [@Thom Ivy ](/edgeware/account/jKauGVPCQkteGTDKuuNwhYhMBrj5QuytgybEC4A5cS4Bki5)unless this is a way of doing some sort of crypto pension scheme for protocol workers?!

Anyways. Throwing down here as a thought starter.

title: Using Elastic Supply Assets to Bootstrap Voluntary Carbon Offsets
body:
**Elastic Supply Background**

Blockchains form voluntary markets to bootstrap new public goods. First with bitcoin, used now as a store of value. Now, [elastic supply tokens](https://www.emptyset.finance/) are able to form voluntary markets for a better medium of exchange. They help resolve the set of problems that are listed below:

- Governments face challenges in establishing the price of money.
- Consumers are searching for yield in a zero interest rate environment
- Need to catalyze a wholesale switch, which requires coordination (or regulation) of a variety of ecosystem actors.
- Securing new infrastructure and settlements layer is capital intense (BTC / ETH block reward / miners rewards)


In theory, elastic supply tokens stabilize around a price by matching supply and demand. Individuals try to speculate or arbitrage around this price, allowing the price to fluctuate based around the target price. If the actual price is above the target price, then supply expands, if it is below the target price, then supply shrinks. _Even if the price is above the target price, it may potentially be rational for an individual to get the token if they expect that demand will continue to grow beyond their entry point._ These coins have grown to several hundreds of millions in marketcap in a matter of months.

Variations on this basic model, change the rate and time between supply expansions or contractions, as well as well as whom takes on the risk or reward of supply expansions or contractions. It also effectively rewards early participants whom help popularize the usage of this asset, as more individuals enter the system, by getting the token, the price moves up past the target price, rewarding early holders. Note there are well known potential attack vectors on elastic supply currencies, such as a [Soros Attack](https://ethresear.ch/t/zero-governance-seigniorage-shares-stablecoin-using-uniswap-v2/7471).

Distributed ledgers are capable of coordinating behavior and resources globally.
One hurdle to mass adoption: how do distributed ledgers reliably interact with the legal world of corporations, courtrooms, and bank accounts?

Its completion would permit Edgeware users to create legal entities within minutes, for free*; protecting their assets in a low tax jurisdiction. It would similarly allow multisig and DAO users to wrap their projects in legal entities, affording them the ability to create legally binding contracts and open bank accounts.

Edgeware is already situated at a 'bridge': Polkadot. By building a 'LexBridge' to the legal world, Edgeware would be strategically positioned to bring Web3 to the world.

title: CoreDAO: A consensus building entity for the Edgeware core community
body:
**UPDATE 1/20/2021: Have been discussing this proposal with community members individually. Will only move forward with it if there is very broad interest from multiple groups of constituents.**

_This is an outline of an idea I've been developing over the last week - if there's enough interest, I'll go into more specific discussions to figure out a final proposal with specifics._

One of the challenges of Edgeware governance is that it's difficult to effectively measure the community's opinions, when the community is highly decentralized.

EDG holders have expressed that they don't feel knowledgeable enough to express their opinions at length, on Telegram or Commonwealth, or through voting on referenda.

We've gotten good results (30+ votes) from polling the Telegram group, but those results are not high-quality enough to be useful in guiding policy.

Kusama solves this problem by establishing a council of major token holders, who are all highly engaged with the project - however, because Edgeware distributed to a much wider community, this model doesn't work for us.

## CoreDAO

I'd like to propose the formation of a **nonbinding congressional DAO starting with ~15-20 core members.** Basically, a decentralized organization open to any natural person (physical human being) who has contributed to the network in some capacity. [1]

The DAO would field one survey per week, usually a single question, distributed to all the members to vote.

**Everyone in the DAO would be expected to vote, every week** - not missing more than one proposal in a row would be a requirement to maintain "active membership" in the group - but it would be acceptable (and perhaps common) to abstain.

- Resolutions on a single issue ("Should Edgeware fund [a project]?") would seek a 1/2 majority.
- Resolutions for policies the network should follow on an ongoing basis would seek a 2/3 supermajority.

title: Discussion: Long-Term Treasury Inflation Reduction
body:
There's been a common call to limit overall inflation for the average stakeholder. However, the treasury is still useful as a long-term resource for the ecosystem. 

Overall, this proposal has the effect of boosting _real_ (not nominal) rate of return from 8% (lower due to treasury inflation) to 16-20% long-term (because treasury inflation will be zero). 

Additionally, the treasury will be able to accumulate rewards by participating in the system itself. At 20-25% of the network participating, it would have a natural “endowment” of 3 - 5% of inflation + fees to run the chain indefinitely and increasing the security of the chain. This can further be tuned by setting the % fees that go to the treasury.

If treasury inflation is used, it should be used to allow for a "perma" slot on Polkadot.

**TLDR Proposal:**

Executed over a few years. 

1. **Grow the treasury to 20-25%** of the chain to the treasury with inflation, like Synthetix or AAVE (DAO). 
2. **Move treasury inflation down** from 62 per block for treasury for two years, then drop to 32 per block, the going to zero.
3. **Use treasury to earn 20% per year by bonding as a validator. **At 20 - 25% of the network, this will let the treasury act as an endowment, earning some of 3 - 5% of the network each year, and continually fund core activities, all while reducing treasury inflation. 
4. **Only turn on any additional treasury inflation for leasing / acquiring DOT. ** We should try to acquire enough DOT / KSM to never lease again.


**In-Depth Proposal:**

We are trying to balance a few interests:

- **Validator Economics: **Make sure that this is high enough, in the absence of fees, that chain security may be guaranteed, I.e 50% of the network or more may be staked. Probably needs to yield some 20% before being moved down as fees pick up in years 2 - 5.
- **General Token-Holders**: limiting overall dilution and giving more certainty around supply if a person is not staked. A person may want to use the tokens ac

title: Protected Contracts and Transaction Fee Subsidies
body:
Edgeware should allow a 3rd party to completely subsidize or pay transaction fees on behalf of users (i.e a protocol team or treasury) for a certain period of time. These are not fully fleshed out, but present some ideas to explore. This area seems relatively underexplored. Any radical change like this seems extremely unlikely to be added to Ethereum, and seems better for an opinionated network like Edgeware.

**Why Adopt Something Like this?**

- Zero fees are the best user experience and can increase usage for protocols.
- Differentiated fee model should work for different use cases (I.e as Edgeware supports social, overkill for users to pay for every TX)
- Would create a clear reason to onboard existing teams into the Edgeware / Polkadot Ecosystem (feeless side-chain with access to Polkadot Ecosystem) 


Even though Edgeware has a wide distribution, protocols, and applications built on top and their eventual users. At worst, getting access to the underlying network token is an inconvenience, and at worst is a challenge for users. This model works relatively well when users are used to paying a fee, I.e in DeFi. We are used to paying a transaction cost associated with every transaction. On Ethereum, transaction fees are killer often pricing out smaller users, this is already why some people are thinking of moving onto Edgeware.

Second, for certain applications, the act of signing a transaction itself can often break a user flow. If for a decentralized social network, I had to sign for every interaction using Polkadot Extensions or Metamask, that would be a deal-breaker. 

How can we completely do away with fees for some contracts without breaking the whole chain?

There is some existing precedent for abstracting away these fees:

1. There are some ways to abstract this. [Metatransaction on ETH and xDAI](https://www.xdaichain.com/for-developers/developer-resources/meta-transactions) allows a user to sign a message, where then a 3rd party pays the cost of the trans
