title: Edgeware as an Incubator
body:
If you're reading this from inside the US, you may have received your Yangdollars stimulus check fiat airdrop by now. Or perhaps not quite yet. The distribution of dollars hasn’t gone quite as smoothly as one would hope. It’s with this context that Edgeware heads in 2021, which feels like the true start to the decade. It's never been more clear that society needs an upgrade. 

Lucky or unlucky, the tailwinds for cryptocurrency adoption aren't slowing down. In ten years, crypto may have gone through two additional price-development cycles, where assets in crypto may be a few orders of magnitude greater than they are today. 

So what should Edgeware doing this year to help this future happen faster?

With an upgrade, we should have new ways of organizing squads to create wealth giving everyone ownership, new ways of storing and safely moving money and IP, and new ways of recognizing individual contributions with financial and social rewards. Each of these ideas has a founder, a community, and a set of crypto primitives that are needed to support them. We just need to facilitate these **let new things happen**. 

Basically, I think Edgeware just needs to continue to work on inviting in independent, technical, and creative individuals. If we bring in these people and give them the engineering, community, and financial tools, we are successfully acting as an incubator--an ecosystem for **new things** to start and grow quickly. Think about YC— that’s turned tens of millions into hundreds of billions of startup value. Each YC company is tackling an incredibly difficult problem with very different personalities at the head of each company. There’s a tremendous amount of activity going in on Edgeware, one look at the [Commonwealth starter thread](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/959--new-to-edgeware-start-here) will tell you that.

title: Solang Solidity Compiler
body:
# Solang Solidity Compiler

I'm the creator of [Solang](https://github.com/hyperledger-labs/solang), a solidity-to-wasm compiler. Using Solang, existing Solidity code can be compiled to wasm. Solang itself is written in rust, and uses llvm to generate optimized wasm code.

The project has practically all of the language covered, now it would be great to have people use it, and report any problems. As it is a new code base there are bound to be issues, like compiler warnings or error messages that don't make sense, or compatibility issues with Solidity.

Since Solang is a completely new code base under our control, we can new features to the language where it make sense. This can be both parachain specific (using chain extension, for example) or more generic features like new crypto functions, or better support for data structures. I'd love to hear some use cases!

[Solang](https://solang.readthedocs.io/) is currently supported by a [Web3 Foundation grant](https://github.com/w3f/General-Grants-Program/blob/master/grants/accepted_grant_applications.md#wave-8---fourth-quarter-2020) (the 2nd grant it received from the Web3 Foundation). To support future development, I am interested in exploring a feature grant.

Thanks!

title: Edgeware Mixer by Webb
body:
Hey all, I'd like to propose my mixer to the Treasury as the first project for my organisation, Webb. We'd like to be the ecosystem partner that manages all things zero-knowledge, starting with a mixer and group pallets that could find utility with identity projects. We plan to make these tools general enough to support application developers building smart contracts so that they could create different types of groups and prove anonymously one's membership in them.

To that end, please leave feedback if any on the proposal. I will attach a roadmap for Webb this year of what I'd like to get done, some of which can hopefully be supported by the Edgeware Treasury.

Proposal:
[https://docs.google.com/document/d/1r1DW0hzW2kYY1oixsvr0AokSGkI3QkNthRoxHO8DMaA/edit#](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1r1DW0hzW2kYY1oixsvr0AokSGkI3QkNthRoxHO8DMaA/edit#)

As has been mentioned by remz, the core utility of a mixer is in the anonymity set. Webb wants to get a v1 mixer live so that we can start building out a great user experience for participating in the v1 mixer as well as begin building out an initial anonymity set. Basically, everyone is in agreement that Edgeware.network makes the most sense and follows category norms for crypto and esp Polkadot ecosystem projects.

## Summary
This is a request for funding for **completed work** delivering "pallet_mint" that enables the direct minting of new network currency (KAB/EDG) to a project team or multisig after a public referendum has been approved.

This functionality is aimed at reducing the complexity of Substrate chains which have so far instituted chain treasuries, where inflation, fees and slashes of validators is redirected into a 'treasury address'.

By minting new currency upon a funding approval, network inflation is directly correlated to the creativity of project teams and the continued benevolence of holders. 

The additional effect is to remove some of the psychological challenges that tend to occur with network treasuries that hold a native currency that fluctuates wildly. When the price is up, spending tends to be more profligate, whilst when the price decreases conservatism creeps in. "Pallet_mint" seeks to overcome short term thinking and prioritise longer term thinking. 
 
## Technical overview
The pallet adds functionality to mint a value on an account, and to optionally mint a percentage of this value on another account (as a fee). It also provides an extrinsic to change the percentage value.

The calls have to be from Root, so as a Democracy proposal, or as a sudo call.

# Decent Partners: Edgeware, Kabocha Structure, Revenue and Growth Strategy via a MetaDAO

## MetaDAO proposal final delivery

This strategy document concludes an applied R&D phase for the [MetaDAO project](This outline strategy marks the conclusion to the ) that was funded by Edgeware two years ago.

> in principle the idea would be to research a range of core issues facing fully on-chain economies that that are setting out to escape centralisation vectors and to create a 'Meta DAO' to address them that benefits from ongoing investment from a range of projects. 

## **Introduction**
Edgeware is an experiment in grass-roots value creation, organisation and funding. 

It's holders are in effect a decentralised association of members, brought together by a successful token distribution event - [the lockdrop](https://medium.com/commonwealth-labs/whats-in-a-lockdrop-194218a180ca). 

90% of the initial supply was set aside for the public which had the eventual and perhaps inevitable result that no one group could dictate a roadmap, leading to the departure of the original founding team to another network. 

This has led to many challenges when attempting to communicate the project's primary purpose, since it doesn't easily fit within category norms. 

This is a good thing. 

Edgeware is different. It is not a pre-defined thing you can put in a box, it is a process - an emergent organism, self-evolving into a vibrant ecosystem. 

It is a digital community, with organisational and economic super-powers that can be tapped by anyone, anywhere with talent, commitment and vision. 

As a result its 'use case' is entirely open to interpretation - what will you build?

Particularly in the crypto space, these folks are being widely excluded from even providing them the basics of crypto education.

It’s our duty to include newcomers into this industry through educating them properly and while there will always be people that are not willing to put in the time, we’ve seen over and over again that there’s many that do want to learn more, but simply can’t find good educational sources to do so.

I believe opening up such a learning opportunity by teaching them just the basics would bring about a revolution in the crypto space.

Our goal with this proposal is to create 21 educational videos geared towards people with special disabilities with a focus on explaining the basics.

# Edgeware & Kabocha locations for contributor events, meetups and hackathons

## **Introduction**
Edgeware first launched its mainnet in February 2020 after the [2019 lockdrop](https://medium.com/commonwealth-labs/whats-in-a-lockdrop-194218a180ca) that created a broad and fair distribution that put EDG into the hands of a decentralised network of members. 

Back then, holding EDG was a bet on the network becoming a parachain and perhaps even more so, as a hedge to Ethereum's scaling challenges. 

Fast forward over two years and Edgeware is slowly and steadily evolving into a grass-roots ecosystem, funding public projects through innovation grants and providing an open door to talented contributors from around the world to learn 'applied Substrate' in an active community setting. 

As the project has evolved, there has been a near constant request for 'events' and ''marketing', however we need to do this in a way that stays true to our core strengths and values.

We need an approach that makes the best use of our broad distribution, ever expanding network of contributors and grass-roots origins to create something unique and differentiated that can build collective value from the (literal) ground up.

# Decent Partners - 2021/22 roadmap, deliverables and funding

## **Intro**

This document summarises Decent Partners' key contributions and developments in Edgeware's ecosystem and a brief overview of the strategy going forward which seeks to double down on Edgeware's decentralised incubator model and position in the emerging DotSama ecosystem. 

## Overview

## Background

Decent Partners' is a UK based limited company focused on developing a '[Network Services](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/discussion/3650-decent-partners-an-introduction-to-network-services)' model within the [Substrate](https://substrate.dev) ecosystem of solo-chains, parachains and relays.

Network Services iterates the existing incubation and partnership model such as that employed by the [Web3 Foundation](https://web3.foundation/) or more traditional startup incubators and corporate innovation studios such as [Prehype](https://prehype.com), towards a democratic, borderless and public on-chain structure. 

Our core focus is the creation, retention and exploitation of novel IP, to drive recurring real world services and licensing revenues that can be shared more transparently, fluidly and equitably to contributors across the full lifecycle of a project. 

We call Substrate based projects that institute this design philosophy _Network Publics_. 

Our mission is to unlock creative potential in anyone, anywhere.

Although not immediately obvious the three oldest Substrate chains are organically evolving from their shared codebases and genesis distributions into a curious family that each offer different pros/cons, cultures and interests.

title: Edgeware: The Grassroots Relay (and spawner of community backed parachains) Network Plan proposal
body:
# Edgeware: The Grassroots Relay 


_Tagline: Edgeware can be the third relay chain, which has a special role, to fund, spawn and support new parachains in the Substrate ecosystem._

After the light and useful discussion we had with Shankar and Thom last week (of May) in the developer meeting, and discussing with filip today, here’s a summary network plan for Edgeware which can be achieved in 6 to 12 months: 

_<this proposal is draft and still being updated>_

## Edgeware Relay Chain with EdgeEVM parachain. 

Edgeware Relay is much more potent in the long term as a multichain framework that has evm capability through its first parachain, than just a smart contract solo chain. 

## Plan

We break down the most challenging upgrade in substrate (erup5), into 3 pieces: 

1. **Edgeware Core Upgrade** - “Edgeware-v0.9.18 OR Erup5" - upgrade of the core system pallets we use day to day; primitives, types and storage migrations.  

2. **Relay Flip** - “relayflip-v0.9.18” - add relay functionality; crowdloan switched off, and all parachains installed through governance (details to follow). 

3. **EdgeEVM parachain** - “paraevm-v0.9.19” - the first of Edgeware’s parachains, EdgeEVM. (details to follow). 

## FAQ:

**Edgeware has too low market cap to be a relay and secure parachains.** If we were running outside projects parachains then this would be a concern. However adding relay and running our own parachain(s) makes no difference to Edgeware’s security. 

**will that mean EdgeEVM has its own cryptocurrency?** Not necessarily, EdgeEVM would use EDG. 

**What about become a parachain on Polkadot?** we can still do this, but the EdgewareRelay can stay a relay and preserve its historical blocks. 

**why be a relay chain?** Short answer is why not? multichain essentialism is a better design than single chain maximalism, aka an all-you-can-eat smart contract blockchain with DApps. This is why a lot of us are here in substrate world to be freed from smart contracts and build cu

There is a burgeoning opportunity to create new ways for music artists to interact with their fans. For fans to become collaborators, royalty distribution and IP ownership, music collectives, fractional ownership of music, etc.

title: Edgeware Community ERUP-5 upgrade update from core runtime developer Flipchan
body:
# **Edgeware Community ERUP-5 upgrade update from core runtime dev Flipchan**

Earlier this year a [proposal was approved](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/discussion/3608-recruitment-of-flipchan-as-edgeware-runtime-core-developer) to address Edgeware's core runtime issues and I (Filip/[@Flipchan](/edgeware/account/mdqwzsGFQ8jq2DQ246a9q3FhUAYKrmvNFEfYALXMWiueijV) flipchan) started on the development.

The goal of this proposal was to upgrade Edgeware's runtime and design structure so that we as a community can follow the polkadot-v releases of Substrate. 

Initially the process of this upgrade seemed pretty straightforward but the difficulty was largely under estimated. 

Edgeware's node is currently not running the official Substrate packages from Parity as they were forked as an early design decision. 

The beginning of ERUP-5 was spent switching to the official version of Substrate. 

Edgeware has an EVM implementation which has not been maintained for a while, causing the code to not be compatible with the latest Substrate releases. 

Edgeware also has its own Ethereum pallet fork (Frontier). I saw after a while that the official version of Frontier was not up to date so I started to rewrite Edgeware's Frontier to use the official Polkadot releases and its currently working and compiling with the polkadot-v0.9.18 branch. 

After this was done, Ethereum had pushed a lot of new updates and several new changes such as new transaction formats. After countless hours of manually upgrading the Ethereum implementation, making sure it syncs with the new Frontier and so on, the problems started to increase. 

After the runtime was upgraded and the Ethereum implementation put in place, which included the Ethereum upgrade that expanded the transaction compatibility. 

During this process lots more libraries started to break and after hours of debugging the node is now building up to the last point where it needs to produce a webassembly build.

title: EVM Benchmarks
body:
_(Edited)_

We've benchmarked the Wako EVM upgrade using the [raymond.release](https://github.com/hicommonwealth/edgeware-node/tree/raymond.release) branch, focusing on the EVM pallet.

The benchmark results are that 1 unit of EVM gas = 3000-4000 picoseconds of execution time, which means the amount of EVM gas we can process per second = 250,000,000.

So far we have conservatively configured gas per second = 8,000,000, which means our block gas limit is 12m gas (Ethereum's is 15m gas). The benchmark suggests we could raise that amount significantly to 250,000,000, which would mean our block gas limit is 375m.

On Beresheet we'll set the block gas limit to 225m, but I recommend running the deploy to mainnet with a gas limit of 12m and will cut a release for v3.3.4 accordingly.

We're going to execute an upgrade to Beresheet that raises the allowable gas per second, and then test for stability by running a few scripts to pack the testnet with blocks. In the meantime we can choose to proceed with the Wako upgrade using the currently configured parameters.

---

To replicate the benchmarks:
cargo build --release --features=runtime-benchmarks

target/release/edgeware benchmark --pallet "pallet_evm" --extrinsic "runner_execute" --repeat 100 --wasm-execution compiled --output /tmp/

cat /tmp/pallet_evm.rs

title: Proposal: Activate the Technical Council, consider EDG as two aspects.
body:
**Summary**
Edgeware was the first Substrate-based mainnet to launch. It deployed not only a smart contract chain but a set of palettes from Substrate that instantiated a council, a referenda body, an on-chain treasury, and several other features.

Since our inception, we've seen Edgeware as one large chain-dao, with the elected council, referenda, and the agency working together to develop the network.

This post argues that we can more effectively describe and manage our ecosystem through a more clear division in our chain-dao concept by focusing on the two aspects individually, analyzing our efforts, governance, and labor separately. 

# Edgeware-as-Chain

Edgeware's smart contract platform and blockchain is a highly technical, cutting-EDG product with evolving Ink!/Rust smart contracting and nascent but highly functional EVM support. With the upcoming Wako upgrade, we'll see a broad ability for Solidity contracts and projects to launch, extend and migrate to EDG.

The process of upgrading to Wako however, has revealed a deep need for technical ownership and leadership beyond what the Agency is currently able to provide. Previously, I'd opened a discussion on an offering of percentage EDG to teams that would effectively develop and sustain EDG's broad functionality with a focus on platform growth and use. Instead, I am proposing that we activate a third governing body: the Technical Committee/Council, which we see active in KSM and DOT governance.

> "The Technical Committee can, along with the Council, produce emergency referenda, which are fast-tracked for voting and implementation. These are used for emergency bug fixes or rapid implementation of new but battle-tested features into the runtime.

title: Why DAOs aren't new
body:
So DAOs are pretty hot right now. 

_Why? _

Because DAOs are organising entities for humans.

Humans who pool resources and then embark on some grand endeavour together. 
That grand endeavour may be starting a cafe, building a pyramid or launching some cat JPGs.
You see grand is all about perspective and importance is a matter of opinion.

When you plug all these endeavours together you get a community.
That's composibility. Interoperability. Bridges. 
That's lego blocks. 
Crypto didn't invent this. 
And you know who invented lego blocks. Lego. 
Crypto just created a new canvas.
A new layer of abstraction. 

Abstraction. This is how our species has conjured _reality_ out of thin air. 

A company is a set of organising instructions committed (originally) to paper in ink.

DAOs are a set of organising instructions committed to networks by code.

Neither is more 'real' than the other. 

Tokens and blockchains are communications technologies.
Just like paper and the printing press.
They are different mediums to tell human stories.

And those stories are games. 
They're experiments to give us something to do. 
That help us figure out our world. 
That make us meaning making machines. 
That give us purpose. 
A reason to get up in the morning. 
To feel alive. 
To feel useful. 
To feel connected.

A company or cooperative is just the ticket to play a part in a certain game.
What's important is the people you decide who to play with.
What values to be guided by.
What intentions to set.
What ambitions to shoot for.
What constitute 'success' and equally what constitutes 'failure', 
When to realise it's [just a ride](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lqv8Os-AdUo&t=4s).

All these things we worry about - linking the real world to crypto. 
The real world is no more real than the world of digital things. 
It's all magic and myth. 
Symbols and spells. 

Money.
Languages.
Towns.
Cities.
Nations. 
Religions. 
All the -isms. 
Every single one is a story. 
A hallucination. A waking dream

title: Developer Experience Update (1/3) Edgeware's focus on smart contracts -- 9/28/21
body:
## Month in advance and beyond

Hello everyone! September has been a big month for Edgeware as we have departed from Summer. There are quite a few things coming up for the developer community on Edgeware, and the posts over the next few days will be talking about some future plans, followed by strategies for developer growth. 

## **Edgeware’s focus on smart contracts**

Currently our smart contracts are able to be written and compiled through the use of both WASM and the EVM. However, as these technologies begin to mature, there seems to be a much greater shift towards Rust, and technologies that are built on top of Rust such as ink!. With this in mind, over the next 6-12 months we will continue building out our EVM presence on Edgeware, providing tools, resources and support. However, after this period of time, we should re-evaluate our options and establish a long term goal, due to the fact that Rust is becoming the more favorable option in this ecosystem. Although EVM is the dominant choice currently, this does not seem to be the case in a couple years as we begin to see more blockchains looking for more sophisticated software to be built from scratch which is hard to do with the EVM. This post will be a couple of highlighted point as to why we should slowly begin expanding our rust developer community, and the amount of resources that we have available from the treasury, pivoting in the direction of Rust and ink! smart contracts on Edgeware. This may prove extremely beneficial in the context of sustainability as it will give Edgeware the slight edge necessary to outperform competing smart contract chains, in turn capturing more of the developer market.

**Why Rust?**

We need a better virtual machine than the EVM (Ethereum Virtual Machine), and especially we need something that is more efficient. We chose [WebAssembly](https://webassembly.org/) (Wasm). This is a virtual machine specification that is intended to match the semantics of physical machines in the re

## Preparing for takeoff -- Dev Experience (⅔)

What we’re trying to best figure out is: **“How do we incentivize people (developers) to build on our platform, and how do we get them to stay”?** The latter of that question is more important in Edgeware's current state. Developer retention is very important as we do not want our ability to bring in developers to be suppressed by a poor **‘Developer Experience’**. This post is to highlight the new initiatives that are currently in motion towards transforming the developer experience on Edgeware into something one-of-a-kind to empower **[Edgeware’s mission](https://edgewa.re/mission)** of serving as a platform for the developers, creators, and members of its community to build, fund and manage their projects effectively.

We want to **provide tools and services on Edgeware** so that:

- Someone **brand new to developing** or someone with **little working knowledge** can begin working with our tools and learn new concepts and patterns to then produce something useful. Edgeware can bridge the developer gap to other tech industries, and learning on Edgeware could be the equivalent of getting an education in blockchain technology from one of the few [elite universities](https://www.technologyhq.org/8-top-universities-that-offer-blockchain-education/) that currently offer any education on the matter. This is can be attributed to the rate at which we’re able to provide new information and support for the latest technologies as soon as they release. The weight of this could be comparable to that of a [CompTIA certification](https://www.comptia.org/certifications/comptia-advanced-security-practitioner) as our merit increases. This would simply be a by-product of the incredible focus necessary to provide an ample suite of tools and resources that will encompass even the most abstract areas of knowledge.

title: A note on Edgeware governance: Clarity, shared values, and a 1p1v committee
body:
There was a discussion the #proposals channel a few days ago, after Thom suggested that we write a bounty to speed up the Wako upgrade, which was very contentious and resulted in the suggestion that I write up some of my responses and takeaways in a document here.

We have arrived at a point where governance discussions are often unproductive. Edgeware can continue functioning in spite of this disagreement (and we are on track to launch EVM within the next few weeks). But this is after many disagreements over the last 1+ year of the network's operations:

- How should we fund core development? (proposal by Dillon, passed, then loudly opposed by remz)
- Should we pursue a Polkadot bond?
- Should we establish an ecosystem partner grant structure?
- Should we establish a technical council?
- Should we focus on EVM or WASM development?


All of these questions had significant disagreements, and I think these disagreements have root causes:

**Lack of a clarity on what Edgeware is providing as a platform**

We've presented many different visions for what Edgeware is. An on-chain incubator, a venture community, a smart contract chain for funding media projects — all of these seem like they do not capture the entire picture.

It's okay that we don't have a single vision (Ethereum never has) but it is problematic that we do not have a way to measure success. We often guide teams in different directions, suggesting to them that WASM is the future, but the WASM platform is also immature and we do not at all have the technical staff to support applications building on it. There seems to be a growing understanding that EVM is a platform we will support going into the future — but Drew and I have made most of the contributions there, and we're increasingly less involved in governance. Can we assure that it will continue to be maintained?

RESOLUTION: We should agree upon a technical strategy, that major members of the network all sign off on, that articulates what we're providin

title: Edgeware is not complicated
body:
[@raymondz](/edgeware/account/mae7JWE1EEMLcno2ZSB8dahwPqVPEyh8zik6dgNpQTvvucq)'s recent post on [governance clarity](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/2140-a-note-on-edgeware-governance-clarity-shared-values-and-a-1p1v-committee) states:

> We have arrived at a point where governance discussions are often unproductive. 

There is a very simple response to all of this which relies on Edgeware's primary decision making mechanism - referendum votes.

We can debate on CW.im all day and propose our own views, in the end, **Edgeware is what it agrees to execute.**

**Of course debate is useful, but in the end, we need to move to a point where there is something to be voted on.**

**Whether it is an upgrade or a funding proposal, there is zero point endlessly debating without there being a community wide vote.** 

Edgeware's culture is derived from what it funds.
Edgeware's technology is derived from what it funds. 
Edgeware's roadmap is derived from what it funds. 

@raykyri outlined the following as key disagreements:

1. How should we fund core development? (proposal by Dillon, passed, then loudly opposed by remz)
2. Should we pursue a Polkadot bond?
3. Should we establish an ecosystem partner grant structure?
4. Should we establish a technical council?
5. Should we focus on EVM or WASM development?


Other than 1, there has been no proposal, just discussions. (Could you pls link to 1 [@raymondz](/edgeware/account/mae7JWE1EEMLcno2ZSB8dahwPqVPEyh8zik6dgNpQTvvucq) )

We have a failure of using on-chain governance to agree things. 

Nothing more. 

The issue with 3, was you can't vote for a structure, you can only vote for a proposal that involves some specific project or team. 

We don't need more debate, we need more community wide referendums. 

That is what our primary focus should be and that is what I'm focused on bringing to Edgeware.

title: Proposal: Offer 15-30 Percent of EDG to a core team, or inactivate smart contracts.
body:
1. Offer an incentive **Update: 15-30%** of total EDG vested to a core team to maintain and improve the network. This could be done through the Treasury modifications Drew formerly proposed where a portion of inflation is automatically distributed to address/es. The Agency would dedicate to marketing this offer, and specifics can be negotiated by the community through the proposal process, but I would want these funds earmarked.  This number is comparative with Messari's research on viable and popular chains. **Update: **This number seems large, _and it is_. It takes into account EDG liquidity and price, and the ability for teams that can maintain EDG and their opportunity cost (simply launching a chain on their own.)  I do not think this is the path we will take, but this is what I think would be necessary to get the ROI we want out of smart contract development. 


OR: 

1. Disable the smart contract functionalities of EDG, as we cannot maintain them nor reasonably guarantee performance or security. At a later time, if and when we can maintain and improve these with some confidence, a network upgrade could activate them. There are bugs in the EVM currently that should be addressed, or the pallet deactivated.
2. Immediately payout all development-focused grants to teams who were building on smart contracts, skipping all milestones.
3. Rebrand the chain as a community investment and benefits DAO with its own validators and security provision, whose collective bargaining power and token onramps can allow individuals to fund public and social goods. title: Interest in partnering to develop University substrate knowledge and participation
body:
Hi folks, I am new here - but have been lurking in your Discord and perusing this discussion forum for some weeks now.

Firstly, a little about me. I run the final year IT product development program at a major university in Melbourne Australia that works with about 2000 students a year, working on 50+ products. In addition to this I am also deep down the rabbit hole of DeFi, blockchain and was an early participant in the Polkadot ICO (which makes up my largest holding). So I have some interest in Substrate based projects (disclaimer).

Being down in little old Australia, we are quite a long way away from the blockchain epicentres of Berlin/Europe, SV and places like Singapore etc. In my opinion we have been frustratingly slow to adopt and understand the importance of blockchain technologies. Over the past couple of years I have been working with academic colleagues to introduce some blockchain units to our curriculum, which is great, and course directors are starting to realise how big this space is and so there is now talk of adding more units for students to take up. We have obviously started with Solidity basics like everyone else, however Substrate has piqued the interest of some of my colleagues as we would like to get more RUST based programming in our courses.

One of the most difficult challenges with building curriculum in this space is that most academics are not up to date with the content, and most of their research and teaching has been in Web 1/2 technologies. There is a quite a steep learning curve for them - and quite often they get some of the basics wrong in the materials they develop, which is obviously not good when we are teaching! 

I'll be frank, some of the discussions here suggest to me that Edgeware is at a bit of an inflection point. It seems the protocol is unsure about its core purpose and how it fits into the larger Substrate eco-system. title: Developer Experience Update (3/3) -- Evolution
body:
Hello everyone!
It's been a while since our last update, this is a pretty large one, but there's a lot of good information, so I recommend reading this thoroughly.

We’re beginning to find our stride, and we’re currently moving with the bull market. To be able to sustain the growth we’re currently experiencing, as a community over the next month it’s really important to begin coming together and notating similar parallels across all different working groups, and how Edgeware will fulfill the missions for all of them. 

We want to ask ourselves the following questions: 

**how should the Edgeware network continue to expand and develop over the next 5 years given our current state? How will our new roadmap begin aligning with newly emerging technologies, and how will we ensure our scope is large enough that we are not cutting ourselves short.** It’s important to understand exactly what Edgeware is capable of right now, and then we can begin to strategize the necessary tools/suites designed to best align with what the DAO believes Edgeware needs. 

Currently, development efforts are focused on our EVM documentation, and support guides for building and troubleshooting in different Ethereum environments with Edgeware in preparation for our WAKO upgrade. Additionally, we are providing more instruction and guides for building within Substrate, so teams looking to build on top of Edgeware are familiar with how the whole tech stack works.

**Cohorts**
Edgeware will begin having a class every 2 that falls on the off-week for the EDG developers call starting the 16th of November. The goal is to teach ambitious individuals that are interested in learning more about blockchain technology, and a way for groups of learners to interact and build with each other. 

This would emerge within our EDG students Working Group, and begin to lay the foundations for a more ‘formal scholar’ system on Edgeware. Tentative meeting times would be 2-hour sessions, twice a month, and cover the like

title: Develop our communal roadmap with Feature Requests
body:
In community-owned projects and networks, no single authority can dictate where it goes, instead, the direction emerges over time through our funding and open-source developments.

 This section is intended to help track issues and features we'd like to see in the network. When items are popular, grant-writers and bounty-curators can fulfill them. Additionally, we can plan node upgrades and releases around hotly-demanded improvements.

 In short, a democratic eature request section is (I believe) essential for developing open-source and community-owned networks.  

To submit, post like normal, and add as many details as you'd like- being short on details. Be sure to vote on others ideas! In the future, it could also be interesting to stake towards feature requests, with backers of activated features winning treasury-spends or a lottery!

title: Climate Bonds
body:
The idea is derived from war bonds, but in this case the bond only pays back the principal sum if a specified climate target is met. For example if the global temperature rise is kept below a certain threshold after 10 years or carbon in the atmosphere is kept below a certain ppm the smart contract will pay back the principal to the lender. The capital raised is then invested by an elected council - preferably a group of people with a mixed skill set covering venture capital, wealth management, technology, climate science etc. Just as the Edgeware treasury invests in blockchain projects this council would invest in a green future, and because the smart contracts only pay out if climate goals are met we can be certain that all the voting rights are held by people who actually care about the climate, so the council will only be beholden to them.

I think the world is more valuable when it's not a desert wasteland so I'm trying to think of why that's not already reflected in our economic systems. These bonds would flip the tragedy of the commons on its head as it gives a financial incentive to improve the commons.

I don't have the skills or expertise for a project like this so I thought I would bring it here and see if there is any interest in it.

title: Edgeware's emerging community 'roadmap'
body:
## A few quick reminders 

At nearly [9m blocks](https://polkadot.js.org/apps/?rpc=wss%3A%2F%2Fedgeware.api.onfinality.io%2Fpublic-ws#/explorer) processed, Edgeware is the second oldest Substrate mainnet chain after Kusama and predates even Polkadot, the two most valuable networks in the whole Substrate ecosystem. 

Both KSM and DOT are **relay chains**, therefore Edgeware is the **oldest and most experienced** Substrate solo-chain in existence. 

Edgeware launched via the lockdrop - there was no token sale, with over [2.2m ETH](https://twitter.com/zhusu/status/1167939840467324928?lang=ca) either locked by individual accounts or signalled by smart contracts holding ETH including Parity's locked multisig, Binance, Coinbase and Aragon. 

It is worth noting that Binance and Coinbase have still not listed Edgeware and so that large distribution is still in yet to be released - there is no reason to think that it will not happen as Edgeware becomes more established. 

The original plan from the launch team Commonwealth Labs was for Edgeware to become Polkadot's first parachain, with a value bearing test-net 'Hedgeware' on Kusama, with a primary focus on becoming an **[ecosystem incubator](https://blog.edgewa.re/edgeware-2020/)**. 

Due to the lockdrop distribution, which offered 90% of tokens to the public, these plans became the subject of public debate, as a community of tokenholders and also grant recipients emerged with their own ideas as to the best direction for the community, this had the effect of removing Commonwealth Labs' ability to make unilateral decisions with regard to funding and governance. 

**This is a feature of Edgeware, not a bug. **

## Commonwealth Labs move on

In the last few weeks, Commonwealth Labs have announced a move to offer core-development to [Astar](https://astar.network/) - formerly known as Plasm network, who also conducted a pair of lockdrops as part of their launch that saw [150k ETH locked](https://lockdrop.astar.network/#/lockdrop

## **Kabocha crowdloan campaign strategy - discussion**

This post relates to Kabocha and our strategy for securing a slot on Kusama by acquiring enough KSM to win an auction.

The key question this post addresses is a simple one...

_**In order to acquire the KSM required, should we encourage our community of EDG holders to also contribute KSM to the crowdloan in return for receiving their KAB?**_

## **UPDATE: Monday 13th December - Poll live. **

If the answer is **NO**, then we will continue as before. 

If the answer is **YES**, then the follow on question is: 

_**How do we do this in the simplest, fairest and most community oriented led approach possible?**_

We want KAB to happen, so we need your input / ideas and feedback and we'll update this post as we go.

If you haven;'t already please read the following so you have context. 

[Kabocha (KAB): A Kusama Parachain Project by Edgeware ](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/2363-kabocha-kab-a-kusama-parachain-project-by-edgeware)

> _We will be delivering the Edgeware community into the Kusama ecosystem through an 100% undiluted distribution for Edgeware token holders. _

title: Solo Contributors' Union (SCU)
body:
**Summary:**
**	**Solo Contributors’ Union aims to reduce the friction from the solo contributors’ side as well as the on-chain governance side for the monthly incentives and to disburse them promptly and under an equal scenario.

**Problems: **
- Limited bandwidth for proposals: With the decentralisation of the agency (one of the major contributing teams) in the coming months combined with the limitation of the external queue, the referenda stage could be bottlenecked leaving near to no bandwidth available for other kinds of proposals.
- On-chain governance can’t process the incentives at once and thus creating differences due to price/market momentum.
- Funding for multiple months is not reliable at this (growth) stage and if the market goes down, the contributors would need to propose a top-up proposal.


**Solution:**
- Introducing 'Solo Contributors' Union (aka SCU)'. SCU will allow the contributors to acquire the community mandate through their initial/first month's proposal and then be a part of SCU from next month.
- Clubbing multiple proposals together: The total amount in EDG will be calculated based on the 7-day average of the total monthly incentives of all SCU members.
- A new multisig will be set up on the 24th of every month if there are any new members added to the SCU. This could be replaced with the multi-sender EdgeWASM smart contract in future. But until then, the multisig threshold ratio will be determined as follows:
- If n = Total number of solo contributors in the SCU,
- And ⌊⌋ represents ‘[Greatest Integer Function](https://www.cuemath.com/algebra/greatest-integer-function/)’,
- Then, the multisig threshold ratio = ⌊(n/2)⌋+1 : n
- To avoid manipulation using multiple accounts, the _primary threads_ with the topic “Solo Contributors' Union” will need a minimum of 100000 EDG holding to post/comment.


**Criteria:**
- Only solo individuals and smaller groups with no hierarchy (ex: Community Mods) will become members of the Solo Contributors' Un

## Summary

This proposal seeks funding to recoup costs for the acquisition of a Kusama 'para thread' by [@Ramsey](/edgeware/account/k43sLKozrmQq7d7aqpYCzqiUM7DJgMaMrVsrY1uPQvpZLWT) which is secured through a refundable KSM registration fee and follows the acquisition of the [Kusama Para-ID](https://gov.edgewa.re/discussion/3759-proposal-kabochas-paraid-deposit-for-kusama) deposit.

This is one of the last stages before the launch of a crowd loan, acting as an on-ramp for new parachains into the relay.

> Parathreads are an idea for parachains to temporarily participate (on a block by block basis) in Kusama security without needing to lease a dedicated parachain slot.

You can read more about para-threads [here](https://guide.kusama.network/docs/learn-parathreads/).

Here is [the outline](https://docs.substrate.io/how-to-guides/v3/parachains/connect/) of the process for securing a registration and working out the correct fees.

Decentration - jBshCuzLrPGmE6tEQJsZLTkPnhTsb4cMchttKafzzRSXNMC

## Funding request

As of 12th April 2022

1 KSM = £122 (spot price w/ 10% contingency)
60 KSM = £7320

£0.0039: calculated using the [7 day trailing average](https://replit.com/@thomivy1/7-Day-Trailing-Avg-dollarEDG)

Total EDG = 1,876,923
+ 10% network services
= 187,692

Total EDG = 2,064,615

## Funding terms

The 60 KSM will be returned to Edgeware if Kabocha does not secure a slot and at the end of 48 weeks if Kabocha does not secure a second year as a parachain.

If Kabocha retains the slot for a second year, the 60 KSM will remain locked.

title: Bounty Parameter Optimization
body:
**Introduction**

This post is about a proposal to modify an existing governance parameter related to the bounty process, i.e. the Bounty Payout Delay which is currently set at 7 days. In short, we’re proposing this delay be reduced to 5 days.

We’ve discussed the complete process about finalizing the new delay (5 days) below.


**Problem Statement**

As we know that in Edgeware the bounty process is designed as follows: 

a. First, there is a council motion to finalize the bounty (1-14 days)
b. Then, another council motion to assign the curator (1-14 days)
c. The Bounty Update Period(1-30 days) - this is when contributors shall work on the bounty task, and the curator can close the bounty if the task is successfully completed or can update the bounty if the goal is not achieved in the given period
d. Then comes the Bounty Payout Delay (7 days). This is when any community member or a council member can come up with objections if any and can reverse the bounty.
e. The treasury spends cycles(3 days). This is a predefined period for treasury spends and the bounty will be paid according to the period.


Now, in step ‘c’, when a contributor completes the bounty task and the curator has played his part by verifying the work, it is not appropriate for the contributor to wait for another 7 days + (0-3) days depending on the spend cycle, to receive the rewards he’s entitled to.This is a bit unfair to the recipient of the rewards as his work, would have already undergone a certain level of scrutiny by the curator.

Also, in those 7 days the price of EDG may undergo some upward/downward movements, and this may cause some losses to the contributor because of the payout delay. 

Now, on the other hand, any community member should have the right to raise objections (if any), regarding the successful completion of the task. Thus, we cannot completely do away with this Payout Delay. 

So, an optimal solution to this would be to set the payout delay to such a duration where,

title: Treasury Tip: Voluntary contribution by a whitehat bounty hunter
body:
This is an appreciation post for the voluntary contribution of reporting the possibility of email spoofing for the Edgeware Agency email. The contributor tipped us off about a setting in the Edgeware Agency email DNS that would have allowed spoofing the agency emails. 

The details are mentioned below:

The issue is related to Misconfigured DMARC on Email Domain.

Bug classification :   Server Security Misconfiguration < Mail Server Misconfiguration < No Spoofing Protection on Email Domain description :

What is DMARC?

Domain-based Message Authentication Reporting and Conformance (DMARC) is a free and open technical specification that is used to authenticate an email by aligning SPF and DKIM mechanisms. By having DMARC in place, domain owners large and small can fight business email compromise, phishing and spoofing.

Why Use DMARC for Email?

Email is involved in more than 90% of all network attacks and without DMARC, it can be hard to tell if an email is real or fake. DMARC allows domain owners to protect their domain(s) from unauthorized use by fighting phishing, spoofing, CEO fraud, and Business Email Compromise

steps to check:

Visit the url : [https://mxtoolbox.com/SuperTool.aspx?action=mx%3aedgeware.agency&run=toolpage](https://mxtoolbox.com/SuperTool.aspx?action=mx%3aedgeware.agency&run=toolpage)

You can see : No DMARC record found

**Short description:** Ongoing costs for the running of high performance, scalable, and reliable public infrastructure for Edgeware Network.
[Full details of proposal is here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1UqscXLJnhM0X18qxF8apROEVMeLzG5GP9TlGZWpKTiE/edit?usp=sharing)


## Original Motivation
Setting up blockchain infrastructure is difficult, time consuming, and expensive:
- It requires a level of server development expertise that many do not have
- It’s costly to run a full node nearly continuously, especially when your dApp’s traffic is low and inconsistent.
- Running production level infrastructure is especially tricky. You need to autoscale quickly to handle bursty traffic, and you want to provide services in different regions around the world to provide low latency services - all of this is incredibly costly, but comes with significant economies of scale for a provider.
- DevOps requires constant attention - time that would be better spent elsewhere building.

A shared node API service helps mitigate these barriers of entry to trying accessing a new protocol by reducing all these costs to near zero. We manage all the nodes for our users and distribute them across the world (with intelligent routing) to achieve global scalability from day 1, we monitor each node and ensure that they meet certain service levels, and we have the expertise and scale to handle production workloads and high peak traffic.
In summary, we try to reduce the pain of getting started on Edgeware Network and minimise the costs of accessing secure nodes while traffic from your dApp is low. When you grow, you can continue to use our shared API service, or we also provide access to one click deploy dedicated Edgeware nodes to any cloud of your choosing.

title: Changing governance time delays
body:
Putting forth some feelers for changing the times. Lately, as everyone is aware, we have not properly used the fast track mechanism and have had to use the normal 3-week waiting time for proposal, referendum, activation. Is there any interest in shortening these parameters in the next upgrade?

The parameters are defined [here](https://github.com/hicommonwealth/edgeware-node/blob/master/node/runtime/src/lib.rs#L460).
The existing parameter set is:
1. 7 day launch period
2. 7 day voting period
3. 3 day fast track (requires 10+/13 council member threshold)
4. 8 day enactment period.


For starters, we can:
- Reduce the launch period to 2 days
- Reduce the enactment period to 1 days.


Do people have more conservative estimates for what they'd like that are at least faster than what we are currently using?

title: Proposal: Re-denominate EDG to a lower supply.
body:
Recently, several discussions about inflation, token supply and price have entered the economics TG group- and we are at a pivotal moment for addressing these, with finality restoration pending and no official exchanges launched. Regardless of your views, this is probably a timely discussion:

**The claim: **5 billion EDG initial supply is psychologically too high for some people, and Edgeware would have a better user experience and bootstrapping process if we re-denominated it. 

For comparison, 
- XRP at one point had 41 billion+ supply, 
-  Polkadot started at 10 millions but re-denom'd to 1 billion. 
- Ethereum, the leading smart contract platform, was est. 112 million ETH in August 2020.



**What is Re-Denomination?**
The proposed redenomination is similar to a _reverse_ stock split, (or stock consolidation):  "Similar to a share split, a redenomination ordinarily alters the circulating supply of a token while market capitalisation remains unchanged."

 So, for example, if you had 100 EDG at 5 Billion supply before, you would have 25 EDG at a supply of 1 billion. 
Notice that the value share you hold of the token economy remains the same, but the #s themselves are decreased. 

Previously, Polkadot did this in the reverse (like a normal stock split,) going from 10 million to a round 1 billion. It also reduced the decimal places from 12 to 10- we would do the reverse here, I believe? thats up for an expert to remark on. 

DOT also experienced some issues as large exchanges like Binance and Kraken did not redenominate at the community-prescribed day, resulting in confusion and likely abuse to their users interested in purchasing or selling DOT.

**The Proposal**

The terms are up for debate, specifically:
1. When this would take effect as a chain-update- preferably before we arrive on T1-T2 exchanges, but not necessarily as long as comms are managed well.
2. The numerical terms of the redenomination. Clearly, community sentiment is to lower the supply, but to wha

title: Draft Proposal: Edgeware Parachain Bonding
body:
The focus of this post ([and the linked full document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1IKWpe4V9JB2TsygE3bbRignjwOLlVnrL2XsetobYyKI/edit#)) is to try and set some bounds so that the community can come to consensus around if and how Edgeware becoming a parachain, some signals to run by the community, and tentative thoughts on making the parachain bonding process more dynamic in the long run. I've TLDR'ed the post here, but there is more context with the Google Doc.

The timing of this proposal going through the treasury is relatively flexible as the parachain bonding process is still rapidly developing--parachain bonding may not be ready until next year. (This would also impact delivery of the Edgeware 2020 Technical Milestone based on this item).

----
Edgeware was launched with the understanding that over time, it would be become a parachain. For the Edgeware community, becoming a parachain has two very direct effects, being able to connect to Acala, Stafi, and other projects with whom Edgeware already has relationships. Moreover, there’s a first mover advantage, this likely means that projects on Edgeware, especially DeFi projects, will be able add DOTs to their protocols which should have a direct beneficial effect on the overall health of Edgeware. Last, becoming a parachain will lower the effective security budget of the chain itself—potentially 2-3x less than the current 10% inflation directed to validators. With Rococo active and Polkadot launched, Edgeware is well on its way to fulfilling that mandate.

In short a potentially viable approach to crowdfund DOTs would be to offer: _**the lower of 1) allocating 1.5 - 3.5% of the Edgeware network or 2) 10- 20% yield in EDG to crowdfund backers. The thought is that we set aside a max portion (3.5%) but if the  EDG/ DOT price fluctuates and the auction is won, then 3.5% may be too much. title: Proposal: Integrate EDG into CryptoLocally
body:
# **Proposal to Fund Integration of EDG into CryptoLocally**

## **About CryptoLocally**
CryptoLocally provides non-custodial, smart contract based escrows for P2P trading across multiple blockchains. It is a community-governed, decentralized marketplace for fiat-crypto P2P traders.

## **Problem Statement and Proposed Solution**
For a typical internet user, the barrier to entry to most cryptocurrencies remains extremely high. To buy an altcoin like EDG or DOT, users normally need to sign up and wait for verification on a centralized exchange, link a bank and buy bitcoin with fiat, and then pay for slippage converting into altcoins. For those in emerging markets, this process is even more of a headache, given that there is a lack of institutions willing to verify those that are typically unbanked. Our goal is to make cryptocurrencies easily accessible to everyone around the world.

CryptoLocally provides a very unique, easy to use, non-custodial solution for P2P trading. People can trade in their local currency by meeting in person, sending a bank transfer, or using KakaoPay, AliPay, WeChat Pay, Venmo and more. As a non-custodial solution, CryptoLocally helps users eliminate the middleman in their trades, and bypass the onerous fees and deposit/withdraw process imposed by custodial solutions.

We would like to become the first P2P exchange to integrate with the Polkadot ecosystem. Given that our escrows on other chains are smart contract based, we see a lot of potential synergy working with Edgeware. We would be listing EDG with the initial integration, which would allow our 25K+ users and the Edgeware, Polkadot communities to start trading the tokens peer-to-peer. We see EDG getting a lot more exposure in our main user bases in Africa and Southeast Asia through CryptoLocally.

We have already [asked our community for their thoughts on integrating Edgeware into CryptoLocally](https://gov.cryptolocally.com/t/using-edgeware-for-polkadot-ecosystem-integration/44)**,**

title: Bootstrapping More Working Groups with Council Help
body:
While still at the idea stage, this has been floated to several community members and received some positive feedback.

Working Groups, initially spearheaded by [@Thom Ivy](/edgeware/account/jKauGVPCQkteGTDKuuNwhYhMBrj5QuytgybEC4A5cS4Bki5) has been a way to help any group of community contributors can come forward and help with the chain in whatever area that they choose. [@mrbulb](/edgeware/account/jXC7ghviUzVcVySg3eD8prB7C9m6VzK6cw2MTyMTDTUye5q) has characterized these as a few different types (agencies, developer focused, interest groups, among others). They're able to receive funds the treasury

However, the current treasury process can be a bit heavy in some processes, requiring a supermajority of the council, or at least a ~21 day (soon to be 10 day) voting cycle for a democracy vote. For smaller grants, $2500 and under, this poses a high coordination cost.

I'm proposing to change the treasury and council pallet to lower these coordination costs by:

- Creating "multiple" treasury proposal types with different thresholds from the council. For example:
- small proposals of $2500 (or EDG equivalent) and under. These would require only a 4 / 13 approval threshold and a 7/13 threshold for vetoing.
- and anything above this requiring the standard 8 / 13 threshold
- Setting a budget per council member per term. For example: $25000 per threshold (or the equivalent in EDG)


It has the potential for some abuse, with a veto limit that is lower than the coordination cost of a "large" treasury proposal it should be mitigated. This also (as is the current) assumes that council members will vote with the chain's best interest. 

These changes would allow small proposals to pass quickly, and also by enabling working groups to get started on their efforts more quickly, this will also likely have the effect of increasing the experiments that can be run on chain!

title: Recruiting developers in residence to Edgeware
body:
Entrepreneur in residence is a common role one might see in the VC world. It is a role that signifies a lot of trust and ability to execute on a given task, be it starting a new company, building a team, and scaling to success. In the blockchain world however, we can get more creative. In fact, I think there's ample room for many "in residence" roles for individuals who want to leverage their skills and have ownership over their time and work.

In this spirit, I think the one of the most impactful roles we can aim to fill would be an _**Edgeware Developer In Residence (DIR)**_: a developer who instills trust through their track record in the industry of developing great tools & products, potentially answering questions and helping other developers, and more. This role would be more open-ended than most, where the _**DIR**_ has the ability to chart their own path in the tools and products they work on, but solely to further the success of Edgeware.
This role could be broken down along a number of different tracks and ideally entirely funded by the Edgeware Treasury. Some tracks come to mind:
- **Tooling -** a tooling focused _**DIR**_ is entirely trusted to build out whatever developer tooling they may use for their own pursuits as well as see fit for other developers in the community.
- **Product -** a product focused _**DIR**_ is entirely trusted to build user-facing products for the users of Edgeware. This could be in the form of faucets or ways of viewing chain data in novel ways.
- **Protocol -** a protocol focused _**DIR**_ is entirely focused on building protocols (if they can manage launching more than one). These protocols would be community run, since they are launched by a paid community developer.


So far, I've explored this idea with a few developers from the Ethereum community and have received decent feedback around its goals and freedom for capable developers. The costs involved directly reflect the quality of the output and so are not entirely cheap

title: Staking Project Update
body:
Hey Edgeware community, here's our progress since the last update:
- Added a new mode to the chain-events listener called archival which allows the listener to poll previous blocks all the way from block 0 up to the current head. It makes use of a rpc call api.rpc.chain.getBlockHash(number) to query past blocks
- The enricher for new session events was revisited and updated to take into account that the events being received are not necessarily at the head of the chain. This incurred a multitude of changes, including:
1. Updating the api call to fetch current era — before the upgrade, api.query.staking.currentEra returned a string, but after the edgeware-node upgrade, the api returns an option — so changes were made to ensure that regardless of which block is being received by the enricher, it should be able to extract the era that the block belongs to
2. Updating the api call to get the validators for the received block. Rather then getting blocks using api.derive.staking.validators() which always returns validators for the session of the header block, retreving validator list using [api.query.session.validators.at](<http://api.query.session.validators.at/>)(hash)
3. Since session.validators only returns the active validator, introduced api.query.staking.erasStakers api call to extract the nextElected validators list
4. To fetch the era rewards points earned by a user, made a separate script that checks the availability of api calls api.query.staking.erasRewardPoints and pi.query.staking.currentEraPointsEarned and returns EraRewardPoints object containing the required data.
5. For fetching details like accountId, controllerId, validatorPrefs, rewardDestination from header block an api.derive.staking.electedInfo call was previously being used. Since this call does not support .at() functionality, we had to fetch all these details from separate api calls including: api.query.staking.erasValidatorPrefs , api.query.staking.validators api.query.staking.payee and api.que

body:

Notes: 
- I have not done anything remotely like a technical feasibility study - this is just a concept to get things started. 
- There have not been any conversations about this concept with Binance, though the aim is to engage them in conversations soon.

## Introduction 
Edgeware is currently in discussions with a '[Top 15 Exchange](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/827-proposal-top-15-exchange-by-cmc-integration-exchange-a)' proposal that requires treasury funds made up of both a listing fee and a marketing fee. A market-maker is also required as part of the offering. 

As a community owned and operated project with a wide distribution and a large native treasury there are challenges and opportunities when it comes to exchange listings.

For example the fact that compliance will be dealing with a community fund, rather than a foundation with a clear legal structure. On the opposing side, with a wide token distribution and active treasury there are all sorts of novel ways that the project can develop and coordinate community listing initiatives. 

This document seeks to spark ideas and strategies around community led listing campaigns that leverage the project’s unique characteristics - beginning with Binance who were one of the largest signallers in the 2019 lockdrop campaign and therefore a key partner in the ecosystems development.

## **Summary**
This is a proposal to cover legal and compliance costs related to the launch of Kabocha's crowdloan. 

Some costs have already been incurred and have so far been paid by Decent Partners. 

We have taken advice here in the UK and are speaking to US law firms to ensure we approach the crowdloan in the most open, transparent and regulatory compliant manner that enables anyone, anywhere to take part. 

Our overall aim is to ensure that the project and its contributors can operate long into the future as sovereign systems with a primary focus on the public good.

## **Background**
Edgeware did not have run an ICO or raise funds directly from VCs, instead launching via [the lockdrop](https://medium.com/commonwealth-labs/whats-in-a-lockdrop-194218a180ca) with a [broad and fair public distribution](https://messari.io/pdf/smartcontracts-q3-2020.pdf). 
![](https://commonwealth-uploads.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/3916cd05-efd1-4632-ab54-632f8680a879.1647984735084)

title: Funding for BillionsDAO
body:
Hello everyone,

we're looking for funding for BillionsDAO. Our focus is to generate an aggregated community of business, tech, and financial professionals, with the blockchain acting as the medium across all channels.

we will need approximately 18000 USD in EDG to fund initial operations for:

 marketing, development, and community management/growth strategy.

We will incentivize Edgeware holders by offering exclusive benefits to Edgeware holders that also claim an NFT membership when they're released.

Traffic from education and events will be routed with Edgeware as well. We wish to create a symbiotic relationship with the Edgeware community and enable our communities to work together to generate value.

## Key Objectives:

**Wealth building**

- Make Money -- Find opportunities in Web3.0 to earn an income, and meet with employers looking to hire.


- Save money -- Strategies, and guides to storing your cryptocurrency by staking, yields, liquidity pools, and algorithmic stablecoins.


- Invest money -- Discover new projects, communities, and tokens to invest in, and maximize your earnings.


**Networking**

Industry talent -- get connected with web3.0 talent, and discover new ways to get involved in the space.

Universities -- BillionsDAO is actively working with multiple universities to create a hub for collaboration and onboarding among college students.

title: Planning: Public Treasury Sale Structure
body:
## Background

We recently had interest from a buyer, (and this has happened before,) for a large purchase of 500k-1m USD EDG. Typically these buyers request an aggressive discount off market price. Currently, there is no holder able to authorize such a sale on behalf of the community. 

In a discussion on Jan 14 morning, the following points were made by various community, I will restate them:

1. The buyer should disclose their identity, their intended purpose of the funds in order to reduce the likelihood that our markets may be gamed by the offer.

2. Time locks would help align these buyers to our long-term success, and this is common with these types of deals. They sometimes bring advisory or marketing support.

3. Buyers should be required to participate in an open auction round, rather than the community entertaining single offers from any third-party.

4. Purchases of any treasury-origin funds by a party should be open, conform to a set standard or be individually approved by democracy process.

5. Discounts should be within a community-approved range or come with certain qualifications, such as logistical support, time locks, or other features that benefit the chain proportionally.


**I open this thread to gather more feedback and points. **

# Decent Partners: An introduction to Network Services

## **Background**
Edgeware was launched in 2019 by founding team [Commonwealth Labs](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2019/03/20/lock-up-ether-get-free-crypto-twist-on-airdrops-attracts-top-vcs/) after[ the lockdrop](https://medium.com/commonwealth-labs/whats-in-a-lockdrop-194218a180ca) secured over 1.2m ETH and participation from [Binance](https://www.binance.com/en/support/announcement/360033342491), Coinbase and established governance projects such as [Aragon](https://twitter.com/aragonproject/status/1122171605734395905).

With no ICO and a broad and fair public distribution that compared favourably to other projects, excitement was high for what Edgeware could achieve as the first smart contract chain and potentially parachain in the Polkadot ecosystem.
![](https://commonwealth-uploads.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/1acd938e-58e7-407f-82f0-c39a082d146a.1643405185693)

From the start it was positioned as a platform to entice ETH holders to a project that would incubate governance experiments through the use of Substrate's low-fees, emerging interoperability and on-chain democracy and treasury.

## The challenge
The project had been positioned as a platform for incubating governance experiments, however the broad distribution ensured Edgeware would itself become the experiment.

With over 90% of the token distributed to the public in the lockdrop, the door was opened to a community of holders who could mediate the decision making powers of the founding team. The result was deadlock between large holders and the founding team who disagreed principally not on what to fund, but on _how to fund _which eventually led to the departure of Commonwealth Labs.

The team at [Decent Partners](https://decent.partners) joined the project around this time, building bridges between both groups and the broader communit

title: Convertible Note Grants: A new funding type idea for the chain/protocol factory model
body:
## The Problem: 
- In the chain factory model, until the incubated chain/protocol gets live, the contributors of the incubated chain/protocol can’t get incentivised from the future treasury of that chain/protocol.
- Price momentum risk: Given the uncertainty of market conditions, the contributors also need to consider the timing of the market rather than just focusing on their deliverables.
- If all the supplementary grants* of the incubated chains are treated just like normal grants, over time altogether they could imply too much pressure on Edgeware’s treasury and sustainability of the ecosystem.


* [The grants focusing on incentivisation of the contributor(s) of the incubated chain/protocol apart from the primary grant are referred to in this thread as ‘Supplementary Grants’.]

## Solution: Introducing Convertible Note Grants [🥁](https://emojipedia.org/drum/) 
- Convertible Note Grants aims to provide the incubated chain/protocol flexibility without any compromise on the incentivisation of their current & future contributors.
- Utilizing Convertible Note Grant, the contributor(s) of the incubated chain/protocol can get incentivised in $EDG and after the full-fledged launch of the incubated chain/protocol and it’s/their treasury, the Edgeware treasury can be reimbursed^ in form of the token(s) of the incubated chain/protocol. This reimbursement is supposed to be done on the chain/protocol level and not directly by the contributors. 


^ [The reimbursement can be preferably done directly to the Edgeware’s on-chain treasury or to a 4/7 multisig with known Edgeware contributors as the signers.]

## Unintended benefits: 
- Multi-assets public treasury: Convertible Note Grants could play an important role in the diversification of the public treasury and thus reduction in the risk of Edgeware the community’s holdings. In future, community grants can also become multi assets’ grants subject to the choice of the proposer to diversify the grants’ risk.

# **Kabocha crowdloan campaign parameters - discussion summary and next steps**

This is a roundup of the various community responses to the [Kabocha crowdloan campaign strategy discussion](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/discussion/2903-kabocha-crowdloan-campaign-strategy-discussion) and associated poll. 

The key question was related to what incentives we should create for EDG holders to also contribute KSM in the crowdloan in return for receiving their KAB. An example idea was for people to activate their EDG amount in KAB by locking a proportional amount of KSM into the crowdloan.

## Key points:

- The general consensus (and poll) suggests people are up for us incentivising EDG holders to also contribute KSM, but this should be an option, not something that is enforced - a carrot rather than stick approach.  


- As a result EDG holders will not be forced to contribute KSM to activate their KSM which feels in line with the overall openness and spirit of the project. 


- To encourage KSM contributions we are introducing **Kabocha Seeds**


- Kabocha Seeds are NFTs that will only ever be offered in this crowdloan and will be central the the governance, organisation, identity, reputation and value capture of Kabocha going forward. 


- There will be a few categories of Seeds available that are designed specifically to:


- Reward work to date from key community members
- Incentivise KSM crowdloan contributions 
- Encourage ongoing participation to the project


- A separate post will follow take a deeper dive into Kabocha Seeds and you can check out the [Kabocha Visuals and Crowdloan NFTs post here](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/discussion/3440-proposal-kabocha-visuals-and-crowdloan-nfts).

Collab.Land leverages the power of identity through crypto currency to create a social space unique to a specific network of humans. 

Once you add the bot to your Telegram group or Discord guild, they will manage your people for you. Depending on their token holdings (fungible/non-fungible) they will be allowed to join the community. If they sell, the bot boots them. 

It has become one of the most widely adopted Web3 tools, providing a vital service for communities to organise their operations. 

This proposal seeks funding from the community to bring Collab-Land to Substrate via native chain integrations in [Edgeware](https://edgewa.re) and [Kabocha](https://kabocha.network) via a 2 year vesting retainer.

# Proposal: Kabocha's Para-ID deposit for Kusama

**Date**
_8th February 2022 _

## **Builder**
[@Ramsey](/edgeware/account/k43sLKozrmQq7d7aqpYCzqiUM7DJgMaMrVsrY1uPQvpZLWT) (Decentration)

## **Network Services**
[Decent Partners](https://decent.partners)

## Summary 
We are entering the final stages of Kabocha's fully community directed and approved development.

This proposal seeks funding for the acquisition of a Kusama 'para ID' which is secured through a refundable 40 KSM deposit. 

A para_id is required to register as a parachain, before launching the crowdloan campaign.

To understand what a para ID is, and why we need it, it's worth understanding the process for launching a parachain. 

From the [Substrate documentation](https://docs.substrate.io/how-to-guides/v3/parachains/connect/): 

> Launching a parachain requires a series of steps to ensure that the relay chain knows exactly what the parachain's runtime logic is once a slot on the relay chain is secured. 
> In order to achieve this, you will need to have previously successfully generated a **para ID, genesis state and Wasm runtime blob**. 
> After successfully registering your parachain, you will be able to obtain a parachain slot (in testing though sudo, and in production via auctions and crowdloans) and start producing blocks.

So what does the para id do?

> You need a para ID to perform any operation referencing your parachain/parathread for a specific relay chain. For example, for providing the Wasm blob or genesis state, creating channels to other parachains for XCM, starting a crowdloan, etc.

In effect the para id is the label Kabocha has within the logic of a relay network that identifies it as a specific parachain.

title: Edgeware Treasury, Value Capture and Funding Terms
body:
# Edgeware Treasury, Value Capture and Funding Terms

This is a post to try and unify a bunch of different discussions, debates and issues that have popped up at different points over the last few months. 

The aim is to open up focused discussion that can lead to establishing a few community standards or at least begin the process of getting people to think through some basic assumptions and principles. 

## Treasury 
 
Edgeware's treasury is/was created through inflation, it is effectively a tax on all holders of EDG established at the origin of the project, with funds assigned to a multisig wallet. 

The treasury also receives funds through network fees, slashing of validators and of proposal bonds if a referendum fails. 

The aim of the treasury is to fund the project's development which is about the broadest remit possible - in principle it can be used for anything the community agrees to fund... hence when someone asks _'What is Edgeware's roadmap'?_ the answer is simple... 

It is what we fund. 

To access funds, proposals need to be put forward to the community via a [simplemajority referendum](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/1563-simplemajority-a-proposed-edgeware-governance-standard). 

The community then votes to approve or reject the request, locking their tokens to indicate their view one way or the other. They can increase their voting weight by locking for longer which gives some signal of their commitment to a particular decision. 
Issues

The main issue is very simple but incredibly complex given the infinite directions the project could take given its current positioning: 

> Edgeware is a smart contract chain with a community-managed treasury, decentralized proposal system and network of DAOs.

This is reinforced by the proposition: **"What Will You Build?"**

# Kabocha: Edgeware grants and recoup

This is a follow up to [@Shankar Warang](/edgeware/account/jA7pLH65zgRNA4UgwqHEWWRxTgg51wuAUgfzmZoYWM2dMVS)'s '[Convertible Note Grants](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/discussion/3670-convertible-note-grants-a-new-funding-type-idea-for-the-chainprotocol-factory-model)' suggestion in which he outlined the following challenge:

> In the chain factory model, until the incubated chain/protocol gets live, the contributors of the incubated chain/protocol can’t get incentivised from the future treasury of that chain/protocol.
> Price momentum risk: Given the uncertainty of market conditions, the contributors also need to consider the timing of the market rather than just focusing on their deliverables.
> If all the supplementary grants* of the incubated chains are treated just like normal grants, over time altogether they could imply too much pressure on Edgeware’s treasury and sustainability of the ecosystem.

And the solution presented:

> **Convertible Note Grants** aims to provide the incubated chain/protocol flexibility without any compromise on the incentivisation of their current & future contributors.
> Utilizing Convertible Note Grant, the contributor(s) of the incubated chain/protocol can get incentivised in $EDG and after the full-fledged launch of the incubated chain/protocol and it’s/their treasury, the Edgeware treasury can be reimbursed^ in form of the token(s) of the incubated chain/protocol.
> This reimbursement is supposed to be done on the chain/protocol level and not directly by the contributors. 

In principle the concept is sound and does address a key issue, however the example that followed felt overly complex and not in keeping with our keep it simple approach to Kabocha.
