title: ClimateDAO
body:
I want to spill my thoughts on what a ClimateDAO can/should focus on and how it can operate. The goal of a ClimateDAO is to donate to non-profits or eventually act as one to do work that benefits the environment.

I think that any given ClimateDAO should have a specific area of focus (ocean/land/sea) as well as a type of action (cleanups/recycle programs/land purchasing). I'm happy to hear thoughts on whether there are alternatives that may be better.

Nonetheless, I want to focus on a land purchasing and rehabilitation ClimateDAO. If DAOs are bound to some legal framework, say LLCs in the United States, then this DAO can likely purchase land. A ClimateDAO that purchases land would focus on the following areas:
1. Finding endangered species and preserving/purchasing the surrounding landscapes for preservation.
2. Purchasing cheap land and growing an ecosystem.
3. Financing projects that involve rehabilitating land from disasters such as oil spills, etc.

The goal of my idea of a good ClimateDAO should be less political and less controversial than I'm sure others can be. The goal is to amass ownership of land resources to preserve and rehabilitate them, providing opportunities for new ecosystems to grow, and preventing industries from being able to extend into said regions.

Feel free to discuss!

title: Recommended Edgeware Network Parameters
body:
We’re right around the corner from the Edgeware network launch--00:00 UTC on Sept 15, 2019, at (8 pm EDT on Sept 14, 2019). At that time, validators are expected to start their nodes and start producing blocks. A few parameters have been chosen so that this can smoothly proceed. You can inspect the [recommended launch spec and node here](https://github.com/hicommonwealth/edgeware-node/). 

In some ways, the Sept 15th network start can be thought of as a soft launch or betanet. At Commonwealth Labs, we encourage the community to lift the parameters once they feel the network is stable. The community may feel that “fully launched” Edgeware will only take a month’s time, the community may decide it will take longer. At the end of the day, Edgeware governance is a community-led process. We detail the parameters below:

- `TransferFee: Balance = 999999999 * DOLLARS`

Fees for token transfers set to 999,999,999 EDG. Recall that the network has 5 billion tokens at genesis. By setting the fee at this amount, addresses will be limited in their ability to perform transfers. Again, in order to enable transfers, the governance process of the network must perform this update.

- Slashing at 0%

The current validators on the testnet are helping to stabilize edgeware-node, in real-time. In the early days of the new network, there may still be unintended events that occur. To mitigate this, the slash percentage will initially be set at 0%, from the standard 10%. 

- `validatorCount: 60`

The current validators on the testnet has produced over 100 thousand blocks--[viewable here](https://telemetry.polkadot.io/#list/Edgeware%20Testnet). We want to make sure that the 6-second blocktime is able to be reached. To ensure that the validator set would be filled for the soft launch, validator fulfilled a [few community guidelines](https://commonwealth.im/#!/edgeware-testnet/proposal/discussion/20) to be included in the recommended genesis spec. title: Funding the Edgeware Ambassador Program
body:
While Commonwealth Labs has quietly encouraged a volunteer-based ambassador team, which we lovingly describe as a thinktank, I believe the landscape has shifted for traditional ambassador programs. As a result of hype-cycles and development cycles being somewhat asynchronous- and perhaps some attention fatigue, I believe we should reconsider the current un-resourced program.

As there is no 'traditional' source of authority in Edgeware (or even several,) the community needs to own the future of the Ambassador program. The best way to do this I believe is to test small amounts of funding for a passionate community leader who can be renumerated for their time and perform nominal operations to recruit, coordinate and incentivize Ambassadors. 

I will personally lend my time to coaching any person who is selected for this role - but I think the best route is to consider an 'RFP' process - request for proposal. While we don't have a formal setup for this sort of thing for the network yet, it basically follows this: 

- We announce a certain amount of funding.
- 'Crypto-contractors' come forward with their plan on that amount of funding.
- The community selects a contractor to utilize that funding. (Ideally, this would be an easy ranked-choice style selection, however, only binary votes are enabled in the democracy module currently.)
- The contractor performs to a set of standards described by the RFP.
- Through some on-chain process or through a second signal or vote, the RFP is fulfilled by the treasury and the contractor is renumerated (paid!)

Regardless of the exact purpose, we should begin to consider RFP procedures for the on-chain treasury. I welcome opinions re: ambassador programs more widely, their usefulness, ROI, etc.

# Questions for Validators
## What is your experience as a validator or node operator?
I’ll be up front and say that I’m not coming from a commercial server operations background – I have 20 years of computer-based mechanical engineering experience. I’ve been running various non-blockchain development cloud servers for a while, for various small personal projects. I have, however, been running a bank of three validators on the Beresheet testnet for a few weeks without incident (other than a few intentional tests to make sure I understand what not to do).
I am also abundantly cautious with updates – I keep my machines up-to-date, but non-urgent updates are done gradually and always tested on non-critical machines first.
## What’s your technical setup? (cloud vs. on-premise; software stack; key management)
Currently, the servers are on AWS virtualised instances, in three different regions with everything firewalled away from the servers apart from the Edgeware P2P traffic. The deployment is based on the Polkadot secure validator project (with a few adjustments to close unnecessary ports), which also allows me to quickly add / replace servers if needed.
They are all running monit for monitoring, which should catch issues early, and they are sending updates to a mmonit server which sends email alerts on detected errors.
Keys are generated on-server, with an off-line copy transferred to my personal machine (and stored on a disconnected USB key) in case I critically need to move a key set to another server - though I would always use the key rotation options for preference if I need to move validation to another machine.

# Edgeware Grant Programme Structure

**Update for discussion 8.10.21**
Below numbers are no longer accurate, but overall structure holds.

## Background

Edgeware's on-chain treasury now controls c. $30m in EDG, whilst other layer 1 protocol DAOs such as Kusama and Polkadot control another $400m more, whilst ETH based smart contract treasuries such as Uniswap control billions. 

![](https://pbs.twimg.com/media/Eym8cenXAAcyHXk?format=jpg&name=medium)

The challenge is no longer fundraising, these projects have enough capital to build for decades. The challenge is now sourcing, developing and delivering quality proposals and rewarding and retaining those that contribute over the long term.

Put simply, capital is no longer a scarce resource, instead the most successful projects will be those that move beyond a speculative and pure product mindset towards the hard work of building cohesive community economies that super-serve their citizens ([see Thom's recent post](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/1101-concept-edg-citizen-benefits)) through well managed organisational structures.  

This might seem like a simple mental shift - but in practice it is a profoundly different way of approaching the funding, development and projects that expand the economy, culture and resources of the chain.

The big question now moves to the scalabiltiy of our funding programme - we need to develop standards, else we will be reinventing the wheel with every new concept or team and have no way to evaluate what is / isn't working which will result in wasted time and money.

## **EDG Grant Programme **

We have had a mixed history with EDG's early funding which is to be expected, but it now feels like the community is at a point where we should discuss and evolve some basic funding structures and processes.

title: Research: The Network State
body:
![](https://1729.com/content/images/size/w2000/2021/04/from-nations-to-nodes-jack-butcher-3.png)
_@jackbutcher: [From Nations to Nodes.](https://twitter.com/jackbutcher/status/1379829485101535240)_

Following [@Thom Ivy](/edgeware/account/jKauGVPCQkteGTDKuuNwhYhMBrj5QuytgybEC4A5cS4Bki5)'s post on [EDG Citizen Benefits post](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/1101-concept-edg-citizen-benefits) this is also a good bit of background reading on [The Network State](https://1729.com/how-to-start-a-new-country/) by Balaji Srinivasen - the rational and phasing is very much in the long term scope of the project and all on-chain protocol DAOs for that matter.

> We recruit online for a group of people interested in founding a new virtual social network, a new city, and eventually a new country. We build the embryonic state as an open source project, we organize our internal economy around remote work, we cultivate in-person levels of civility, we simulate [architecture in VR](https://thewild.com/blog/architect-getting-started-with-vr), and we create art and literature that reflects our values.

> Over time we eventually [crowdfund](https://twitter.com/balajis/status/1269178671086006273?lang=en) territory in the real world, but not necessarily _contiguous_ territory. Because an under-appreciated fact is that _the internet allows us to network [enclaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enclave_and_exclave)_. Put another way, a cloud community need not acquire all its territory in one place at one time. It can connect a thousand apartments, a hundred houses, and a dozen cul-de-sacs in different cities into a new kind of fractal polity with its capital in the cloud. 

> Over time, community members migrate between these enclaves and crowdfund territory nearby, with every individual dwelling and group house presenting an independent opportunity for expansion.

title: Working Group for Legal
body:
I've just joined this community and was looking for the legal working group after seeing multiple mentions of legal issues arising in relation to DAOs and the creation of business entities to help drive growth.

I think it's fair to say that this industry is at a point where these questions are becoming more pressing as communities look for safe ways to manage and distribute treasury funds and deal with the regulatory changes that are taking place around the world.

There is also the important question of providing developers the necessary protection both in terms of the work output and for the platform itself. There are a significant number of legal issues associated with these platforms and it would be good to find a place to explore those issues and identify novel ways to address them.

If there are any other lawyers who would like to collaborate (or any devs interested in these topics), please let me know and we can start up a WG on Discord.

title: Concept: EDGPorts
body:
I've been approached by people who operate traditional businesses, but who would like better ways to integrate crypto into their models- and some also seek funding for public good offerings, but simply not in the digital but the physical world instead.

If we want to pursue a more fair, open, and opportunity-filled world,  our technology should begin to have real-world consequences and integrations. To explore what a localist Edgeware might look like, I'm sharing the EDGPort concept, a kind of embassy into the local.

An EDGPort is a publically-funded brick-and-mortar business in the physical world.  You can imagine them as a set of mixed purpose locations that integrate with Edgeware organizations, offer public goods to Edgeware citizens, and serve as laboratories for the business models of the future. 

Examples of EDGPorts we may explore over the next year:

1. Community-owned and crypto-integrated community theatre model in Berlin, with a warehouse that can serve other needs and community meeting space.
2. Biohacker / Maker space in Austin TX that works on publically funded and opensource medical solutions.
3. Maker and hacker spaces in Japan. 


The EDGPort concept helps facilitate awareness, investment into local communities, capacity building, and community meetups around the world.

We recently funded the PR firm Market Across as one part of the Agency's developing communication initiatives. It is a 3 month contract and will help us drive awareness and interest around the project.

As part of their onboarding process, we have been asked to complete their Q&A document which helps them understand our priorities as a community.

In our continuing quest to ensure an open, accessible and participatory environment we will be developing this in the open.

To kickstart I have detailed a few elements that I believe offer's Edgeware a unique proposition.

**Important note:**

We do not need a thousand specific characteristics - we need a few things that offer the project a 10x advantage that can be communicated via our ongoing outreach and can form the foundations for the challenge of making "Edgeware a meme". 

When viewed through this lens, it is worth weighting the advantages you believe the community has when considering its emerging traits.

- **10x benefit**
- a benefit that is difficult if not impossible to replicate
- this benefit should ideally compound over time
- in general this is about long term thinking
- **example: the lockdrop distribution **
- **5x benefit**
- a benefit that puts the community into a select category of projects
- this benefit may be sustained over time
- in general this is about mid term thinking
- **example: the community treasury **
- **2x benefit**
- a benefit that is currently a small benefit over other projects
- this benefit is likely to disappear relatively quickly
- in general this is about short term thinking

## _**🌶 Pico is a protocol for decentralized exchange built on Edgeware.** _

As many projects are beginning to build on Edgeware, including DeFi protocols for privacy, perpetuals and synthetic options, and undercollateralized lending, and core infrastructure like mixers and NFT ecosystems, we are launching an exchange to help empower these projects.

## **🐣 Origin Story**

Decentralized Finance has become a massive industry and when compounded with the heft of the NFT market, we are seeing the effects of the volume in exorbitant ETH gas fees. Polkadot and Edgeware can offer a solution for these constraints. Pico aims to provide a solid DeFi foundation for the Edgeware ecosystem and reduce gas fees for traders and liquidity providers. 

We are launching a decentralized exchange based on a modified version of the Uniswap core contracts, with a community-oriented token distribution giving 80% of tokens to the community. Additionally, we developed a friendly web interface and a fast, easy-to-use mobile app.

Our goal is to launch a user-friendly product in all senses: interface, speed, transactions, and community. After launch we will continue to be active members in the community and will contribute to the community-led governance and development.

title: Edgeware runtime upgrade: Tokyo-2
body:
Hi everyone,

A critical bug was recently uncovered in the Rust EVM crate used by Edgeware and other Substrate chains, which allows certain transactions to be crafted that could cause nodes to run out-of-memory.

The issue has been patched in the latest version of the EVM crate. We've upgraded the Edgeware runtime to use the updated crate at commit hash **dccb703**: 
[https://github.com/hicommonwealth/edgeware-node/tree/drew-fix](https://github.com/hicommonwealth/edgeware-node/tree/drew-fix)

We've issued a runtime upgrade to update the chain to this latest version. It is currently **Democracy Proposal 33** and, at the time you're reading this, will be in voting as **Referendum 37.**

**EDIT:** We are also working on issuing a fast-track proposal that will have a shorter resolution time. Will update here with more details as that happens. **This upgrade is being voted on as fast-track referendum 38, with voting open through Saturday, May 15 10pm PT.**

title: What is the treasury for? Who should benefit and how?
body:
So this follows a few discussions over a long period about the Edgeware community treasury which currently holds c.$20m - a not insignificant amount of money.

It is available to anyone, for practically anything which offers an incredible new opportunity to fund public goods, infrastructure and as a way to accelerate innovation. 

There are a number of ways the treasury has been tapped so far and a few ways that it may be in the future.

One challenge we may increasingly see is that getting funding from a DAO will be easier but enforcement of those terms will be harder - and there will be many messy arguments as to who bears responsibility. 

As a result it's worth outlining and discussing these things as we experiment - refining processes and standards as we go, there's likely no perfect answer or silver bullet, but we should be open to discussing the ups and downs of each route.

## 1. Grant funding 
Commonwealth Labs were funded with a 50m grant for their 2020 roadmap - you can view the post [here](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/509-edgeware-2020-roadmap-discussion).

This is where things start to get a bit messy, as the 50m grant also included the launch of BuilDAO as part of the deliverables - for various reasons this hasn't happened. 

I really don't know how we should deal with this - 

- Is the 2020 roadmap complete without BuilDAO?
- Did the community get value for its funding with the 50m paid?
- What should we as a group expect from a reporting perspective?


Right now Commonwealth Labs is incubating projects such as Picoswap and Common protocol, but is this what was meant? 

We need a way to come to agreement on this or all the debates and hand-wringing over the Agency proposal, which also exists as a large treasury grant builds on a slightly wobbly foundation. 

What is also uncertain here is whether the funding is for open source work, or for profit - it's a little in between and hence where the waters muddy.

title: Announcing Hedgeware, a Kusama parachain for Edgeware
body:
**![](https://lh6.googleusercontent.com/zB2HQImcbZRcYKMW2ub4vK7-SLXIKMggrlHO8g69zqny03PUrcXeQmRXMHfu5NVAAYeX3ygIihl5EzKb3f1UDGPc2Qcp8kKsKJnb1y4jxOui4jjvn8qd2UgNnJahLMS6mKgMGgoB)**

With the rapid growth of the Polkadot community in the last year, many projects have announced their plans to launch canary networks connected to the Kusama ecosystem.

These canary networks serve several purposes: they are places to deploy new and unproven technology, they support governance experimentation, and they reduce the risks posed by unforeseen events.

For those reasons, **we are excited to announce Hedgeware, a Kusama parachain and canary network for Edgeware**.

The network serves several purposes which are complementary to Edgeware:
- It allows us to experiment with the process of parachain bonding, inter-chain message passing, and building multi-chain Polkadot applications
- It serves as a canary network for Edgeware runtime upgrades, allowing us to identify issues that might not be easily demonstrated on a testnet
- It serves as a parabridge, allowing Edgeware to access early Polkadot tech as soon as it goes live on Kusama


We’ve chosen the name Hedgeware to reflect the fact that this is a canary network for Edgeware, rather than a separate network.

We expect that most Hedgeware activity will go through Edgeware or Kusama. And like other Edgeware DAOs, Hedgeware will have its own distribution of ownership, but it will also serve as an independent chain with a technically focused community.

While Edgeware will continue to be a community-oriented smart contract chain, Hedgeware will serve as a place to deploy and test cutting-edge technology before it’s ready for broader use.

In line with these priorities, the Hedgeware native token HEDG will follow an altered distribution:

- 50% to holders of Edgeware on the snapshot date of May 1st UTC 00:00
- 20% to participants in the Kusama crowdloan and parachain auction. We anticipate that half of this amount will be allocated fo

Edgeware is a state-of-the-art smart contract chain with a community-managed treasury, decentralized proposal system, and network of DAOs.

Edgeware is a platform for the next generation of decentralized applications. On Edgeware, Ethereum developers can deploy [Solidity/EVM](https://main.edgeware.wiki/edgeware-runtime/evm) smart contracts with few or no changes, while new developers can get started with Rust and [WebAssembly](https://main.edgeware.wiki/edgeware-runtime/wasm).

title: Why Hedgeware is currently a terrible idea.
body:
This is a repost of a comment on the [Announcing Hedgeware ](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/1153-announcing-hedgeware-a-kusama-parachain-for-edgeware)post - I felt moved to actually post a longer piece here since I really believe the current distribution makes it a terrible idea. 

I realise most will care about an airdrop of new tokens - and see this as a 'win' but it really is worth considering the implications of the economic decisions taken in Hedgeware with regard to it's initial distribution and how this changes the fundamental nature of 'Edgeware' as a truly community owned & operated project. 

--------

Edgeware's defining feature is the lockdrop distribution - it is the project's one major success and something that confers unique advantages over other projects.

It was a complete one off - a success that surprised everyone - it is very difficult, if not impossible to replicate - many others copied the lockdrop, but none came close.

The distribution was the major attraction to me over any other Substrate project - and is at the core of the reasoning I give to those who I bring to the community. 

I'm going to drop the below here again as a reminder to how this distribution compares with other projects.

body:

_This post was initially a response to a community question on Telegram asking how Edgeware is different to Moonbeam and other Substrate projects - [link here](https://t.me/heyedgeware/44057). _

_This is an expansion of that answer (with a bit more colour and a few more links) and is an aggregation of ideas, insights and contributions from across the community, bringing together many different perspectives into a coherent layered structure designed to pin-point Edgeware's unique characteristics, evolving roadmap and long term vision. _

_It includes many links from across the project and a bunch of articles or essays that have been useful in the past.  _

_This is hopefully useful as a starter for those new to the project as well as those already in the community as a way to join the dots between a bunch of seemingly unrelated things. _

_As always, this is work in progress... keep the comments flowing and I'll update. _

---------------------------

# So what makes Edgeware different? 

## 1. Upgradeable and interoperable blockchain 

First things first. Edgeware is built on [Substrate](https://substrate.dev), a SDK (software development kit) that makes developing, launching, maintaining and upgrading blockchains many orders of magnitude easier than previous generations.

As a result, all Substrate chains share the same basic building blocks meaning chains can adopt the innovations of others built on the same base and also interoperate and communicate via a [Polkadot relay chain structure](https://polkadot.network/technology/).

Substrate unlocks new capabilities for developers, community builders and creators and uses proof of stake to secure the network and also reduces gas fees that have made Ethereum an expensive place to experiment. Substrate chains enable fork-less upgrades that would previously have split communities into competing tribes and als

title: Commonwealth interface grant for Edgeware - Stage 2
body:
The first Commonwealth interface dev grant was approved at the beginning of January - covering support for Bounties, Offchain Polling, Members/Search, and general improvements.

Now we know more about how to make governance work on Edgeware. In large part this is thanks to the ongoing contributions of community leaders bringing forth proposals like these:

- In voting or soon voting
- Zien
- New Futures
- Exit Theory
- Agency proposal
- Not brought forth yet
- Decent proposal
- Pico/EDG liquidity proposal
- Layer Wallet
- Passed
- Webb

- Staking UI


There seems to be general alignment on some proposals - primarily around those bringing new tech and builders to the network. There also seems to be more disagreement around proposals to do with determining the network's strategy, and how we make strategic financial allocations.

With this in mind, I'm tailoring Stage 2 to a few governance priorities:

- **More detailed feedback on proposals.**
- Gathering feedback on proposals is one of the most important functions of our governance system, and our current feedback system relies on forum-length responses.
- It's difficult to keep track of issues in a long forum thread.
- Sometimes we write proposals in separate documents, like Google Docs, but that poses a number of problems - they get updated out of sync with the thread, and sometimes deleted as people move between organizations.
- Commonwealth is a community space and docs are private spaces - it's less natural to provide detailed feedback outside of the "framework" that Commonwealth provides - vs. how people seem pretty comfortable answering Google Docs when they are explicitly cc'ed for feedback.
- Right now, in depth conversation around longer proposals seems to happen productively in private - not really in public.

title: Extending the Power of Public Funds
body:
We've used treasury funds for grants, proposed funding VC-like BuilDAO launches, funding residencies for cultural minds, and more.

The treasury is already showing strength as a game-changer among blockchains when the funds are deployed strategically. The use of funds for the public good is the mandate-  however this does not preclude their application towards private ends, so long as the Treasury gains /more/ funds in the future for continual deployment.  Jam recently discussed Flash Loans, and I believe they meant from the Treasury and this is genius because the treasury is unaffected at worst, and if deployed for the right ecosystem reasons, these loans could increase the value of EDG, spur development and ecosystem building.

At a glance, here is the stack I am seeing unfold:

- Project/Business launches (Grants or BuildDAO- equity, tokens)
- Single-purpose Transactions or Refi/Arbitrage (Treasury Flash Loans)
- Project/Business Exit (Exit-to-Community: Treasury pays, Edgeware citizens benefit.)
- Various others (Tips, Gitcoin-like Matching from Treasury)


The one use case I am not seeing well-served is that of growth. R[ead a nice article from Zima Red's NFT newsletter on Pipe](https://andrewsteinwold.substack.com/p/new-funding-methods-and-markets-for), which basically provides funding to projects ready to grow by letting projects:
- Sell annualized future revenues instead of equity at a high APR
- Investors can also use Pipe as a platform, making financing terms competitive.


The treasury can mimic this by taking ownership of a time-limited future revenues, and also lower the costs of other investors hopping in -- leading rounds of this kind of investment. Zima Red also points at the capacity to tokenize these debt contracts,** allowing the treasury itself to sell these.**

title: Citizen-led Immigration to Edgeware- or Sponsoring a New EDG-holder
body:
**Summary:** In Canada, 5 citizens can raise a meaningful pool of funds and consent to integrating and guiding an immigrant and family for their first year- in a process described as citizen-led immigration. In this post, I show how we can use a similar structure to rapidly grow Edgeware in a selective, non-extractory process that is likely win-win.

When a user first learns of Edgeware, participating in the network requires EDG. Specifically a participant requires enough EDG to overcome the existential deposit to the creation of an account, and also enough EDG to participate meaningfully in voting, proposing, and paying the fees for these actions. 

Most users begin via purchase by exchange, lockdrop or signal participation, and occasionally from grants or tips from the treasury. 

To add to that list, I propose that we offer the infrastructure for pay-it-forward style donations to would-be Edgeware citizens.

Sponsor User Story

1. An Edgeware user voluntarily donates some EDG to a Sponsor Pool.
2. Other users contribute, and every time a threshold of say, 10-100 EDG is reached, the list of users that contributed that batch of 10-100 are linked as a Sponsor Group. Sponsors may receive NFTs or Remarks.
3. These Sponsors ideally join a community channel or receive some organizing capacity either specific to that group or to the full set of Sponsors. 
4. Once in this group, they interact with, mentor and build relationships with new Edgeware users on the system and opportunities.  After some time period, these new Edgeware citizens are encouraged to donate and sponsor another round themselves, the cycle repeats.


On the other side of the relationship..

1. A user expresses interest in participating in Edgeware.
2. The Sponsor Pool of EDG transfers an amount required to pay for attestation transaction fees.

# 
# Upgrade 1
Upgrade 1 moved Edgeware to Substrate 2.0 rc3 within the Edgeware Node v3.0.8.


### Addressing Finality Issues
As it stands, the Edgeware node has been having some issues with validators not voting in the finalization process, leading finalization to stall and eventually triggering forced GRANDPA set updates. Not long ago with the help of [Andre Silva](%5B%3Chttps://github.com/andresilva%3E%5D(%3Chttps://github.com/andresilva%3E)) we merged in some changes to the GRANDPA service worker, and turned off forced finality changes to the Edgeware runtime. These changes will make their way into the first Edgeware runtime upgrade.
For technical details, please refer to:

Additionally, we have repaired
1. Crashes in the v1.0.1 node due to inproper time arithmetic

In order to prepare for the upgrade to Substrate 2, several migrations of data within the chain were included. Edgeware launched with the balances and vesting module as separate modules. title: Bounties pallet
body:
The bounties pallet by Emiel from Polkascan and Bryan from Acala/Laminar has just been merged into the [master branch of Substrate](https://github.com/paritytech/substrate/issues/5713).

I think it would be great for us to get it merged into Edgeware in one of the upcoming runtime upgrades that [@drewstone](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/account/hwR8hAatmmdupBLXQSxLUPBa8GhRomLD9hf6iRtFeXs8fcY) is working on.

The pallet lets councillors propose and fund bounties through a fairly well-thought-out-system (see section 5 in the issue above for a full description of how it works):

- Bounties are proposed with a curator, a description, and amount.
- Bounties must be approved by a simple majority of councillors, its funds are earmarked and held from the treasury.
- The council cannot alter the bounty once it has been approved. The curator is responsible for delegating the work associated with the bounty and releasing it once that's been completed, but there is a delay that allows the release of funds to be canceled through democracy (i.e. through a coin-holder vote).
- If enough time passes without the bounty being completed, the bounty expires.


Once this is integrated into the runtime, it would be great for councillors to get together over a call, ideally one open to the public, to come up with a few solid bounties for Edgeware. For example:

- An implementation of Thom's [citizen sponsorship](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/610-citizenled-immigration-to-edgeware-or-sponsoring-a-new-edgholder) system for new Edgeware members
- [Artists' residencies](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/600-candidate-list-for-artist-residencies-and-orgspersons-of-interest)
- Other projects in line with our [values](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/536-why-are-you-here-edgeware-founding-values-culture-and-focus)

Welcoming citizenships through a sustainable approach.

- One time reward-motivated mindset (of both AMA participants and Influencers)
- Short-term yield for projects
- Reward oriented mindset and generic questions

title: Announcing Sublime
body:
Sublime is a new lending protocol aimed at providing a more diversified and robust lending experience by:

1. Tokenizing borrow positions to provide users exposure to price volatility of the underlying collateral and to self-liquidate.
2. Creating fixed size reserve pools to enable instant liquidations, provide cover in case of adverse events, and enable LPs to onboard new collaterals.
3. Enabling undercollateralized loans against future tokens earned through collateral staking, yield-enhanced tokens, or locked with Sublime to earn SUBL governance tokens.

Link to our first Medium article: [https://medium.com/@sublime.finance/announcing-sublime-f9d6fd1abd2f](https://medium.com/@sublime.finance/announcing-sublime-f9d6fd1abd2f)

We're excited to launch on Edgeware. It's native EVM support allows us to iterate quickly without having to operate a parachain while still being accessible to the Polkadot ecosystem at large.

We would love to hear your thoughts.

Links to our socials are attached in the article. Thanks!

title: More equitable and innovative Blockchain-VR in EDG
body:
From my twitter:
> [an oppressive feature of the financialization of digital land is that resolution standards and scale can be informed by economic engineering. If I can buy a small parcel and build a scale appropriate version of NYC, users should be able to shrink down but scarcity was reiterated](https://twitter.com/thom_ivy_1/status/1311717726432505857)
> 
> placing this into my example box for reiteration failure in new technology. 
> - Why do we need digital land values?
> - How do we charge for access and not dLand?
> - Who benefits from scarcity in dLand

Currently, Cryptovoxels, Decentraland and other major digital-land VR projects quantify and boundary their core resource, but my point is that VR doesn't need to be this way. Using scale (within technological limits) we can have a city on a tabletop, or a planet-sized party room between Earth and Mars.

Don't like where you are? Shrink down and see whats happening in the cellular scale.  

When VR projects come to Edgeware (This is an essential component of my vision for a replication of civic life in Edgeware-  the creation of realistic space to engage.)  ... they should consider more innovative routes of economic modeling for that space- specifically they shouldn't use space as the scarce resource at all. The creation of a cathedral the size of Hungary should not be more expensive than other uses- the value we gain from being able to generate, explore and share such a cathedral is far more important. 

**We have reiterated the capacity for  creativity based on wealth.**

**A potential solution instead of boundaries using the traditional dimensions, is to derive value from the ability to perceive entities. Overlapping projects and cities can occupy similar space, maximizing convenience (although teleportation is built in frequently,) but still be permissioned and financialized.  **

title: a proposal for games!
body:
## Update: Join the working group telegram! https://t.me/joinchat/EEnJ60cK0v316D46KkBmeA

games have been something that I have always gravitated towards, namely for their ability in generating fairness or exploiting fairness toward strategic entertainment. The games I look at below shift from being just ‘fairness’ generators and strategic games, depending on the existence of a ‘wager’, its size, or iterations of gameplay. In recognizing these metrics in their ability to shift the relationship of fairness and strategy, games can be harnessed toward both entertainment and productive ends. 

What’s more, gas fees on Ethereum are currently prohibitively expensive. DeFi use cases are consistently the highest bidder for blockspace. Edgeware has an interesting opportunity to leverage it’s cheap and plentiful blockspace to explore higher volume, lower value transactions. Games of probability and volume are fantastic as they create external value from the sum of participation by testing out the (ir)rational mind of a population. 

random data points about games in crypto: 
- ~2010, there were quite a few poker site start ups unable to get gaming/banking regulation, moved their servers off-shore and allowed no-limit bitcoin poker. This got a lot of people from the cash and gaming economy to take notice of bitcoin relatively early for its censorship-resistance. These IRL bitcoin poker networks are still active, predominantly in vegas where bitcoin/usd trades occur with the use of poker chips as temporary fungible collateral. 
- Erik voorhees’ first business in the space was known as “satoshi dice”, a dice game that used bitcoin to generate the randomness for the game. in the spring of 2012, it famously sold for ~125,000BTC. 
- One of the first internal projects at consensys was “virtue poker”, though regulation was an issue for a long time 
- Fomo3D, a game designed with interesting game theory mechanisms got a bunch of attention and engagement.

## 
## Narrative development

At the root of any narrative development there are typically four key stages.
Insight - Set the scene, introduce the big picture, what is the context to the story you are telling?

Problem - within the context you have framed, what is the primary issue?

Solution - what is the compelling answer to the problem and context you have set?

How it works - explain how the solution works, from high level to deep dive.
This approach gives structure to storytelling and applies pretty much universally - from startups to filmmaking, crypto-networks and even memes - the atomic units of storytelling which bundle context, problem and solution in one image...

Problem - It's hard to see the wood for the trees.

Solution - Edgeware lets you see the bigger picture
This structured approach can waterfall across every aspect of a project, from a helicopter perspective to deep down into the weeds of a complex technological stack. 

Let's take the (simplified) original positioning of Apple.
Insight - Computers will change the world but...

Problem - Right now only software engineers understand them...

Solution - Introducing Apple. We make computers everyone can use.

How it works - An intuitive human machine interface etc

> **Protocols die when they run out of believers.**

## **Introduction**
**This is a phase 1 project as part of the BWG proposal which you can view [here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1DPodqUajc9yzTG4iVGUSMekOtj3BTLMUwYWUUIuZI4M/edit#).**

Generationally influential brands of recent memory have been those that have understood that building long term trust is not about marketing, it is about riding the wave of cultural movements and then seeding that story through influential networks that share common values.

These brands were born into and made famous in an era when TV was dominant and a cultural narrative could be defined and controlled from the top down. 

There is a mistake made by most product companies, especially in a social era, that marketing is analogous to building a community, when in fact the latter is far more about cooperation and collaboration, taking a role closer to the facilitator of a community’s intrinsic ambitions, rather than authors of a marketing message.

## Community Networks
Blockchains are evolving into coordination systems for _borderless community networks_, where cultural narratives are the key driver in the winner takes all tendency of network effects. 

Assuming technical competence, it is likely that over time a cultural narrative also known as a _movement_, will be a far better indicator of crypto currency valuation than any direct comparison of the monetary policy or capabilities of the underlying technology.

## How do you create a movement?
The development, production and distribution of compelling original content that can cut through the noise online to reach and engage newcomers is vital to kickstarting a movement.

title: Using Discord for Working Groups or other  Community Platform Changes?
body:
We currently use Telegram for Working Groups primarily which is convenient:

- Many users have TG
- Many of our community members are most active in Telegram it seems.
- The software is easy to use and quick to load.

It also suffers from bots, not unlike Discord but Discord may have more tools to prevent abuse.

Discord on the other hand, has one MAJOR advantage: Channel management.  We can quickly spin up sub-units of communities whereas Telegram doesn't nest groups.  We also heard from other protocols which had begun using Discord voice chat channels for meetings, rather than Zoom. On the other hand, we have a councilmember who is against Discord for privacy reasons and these also seem salient to a cryptocurrency project.

An aside: It would be amazing to have the 'send to whole channel' function of Slack built into subchannels -- imagining a Working group being able to 'bubble' up an especially important conclusion to decisionmaking to a parent channel. I suppose Telegram uses Forward for this.

We can continue to bridge channels, of course - but opening a discussion on what our native platform should be and also how we use Zoom right now. Some projects prefer the open source Jitsi.

title: zkBridges
body:
Toying with an idea where bridges are themselves privacy mixers. The basic premise is:
1. Sending assets across the bridge can be claimed by any account that presents a signature of knowledge over a discrete log, hash preimage, etc.
2. A depositor can repeatedly withdraw arbitrary sub-values for a given bridge transaction. This preserves sender/receiver anonymity by making it harder to reconstruct matching inputs/outputs.


Not sure I've seen prior work in this direction and interested to continue sharing thoughts, formalisms, etc. I see the main problem as figuring out how to preserve anonymity on the receiving end.

More formally, consider a real number _**r = r1 + r2 + ... + rN**_. For a bridge depositing transaction of value _**r**_, we want to enable a receiver to withdraw from the bridge any values _**r_i**_ while preserving sender/receiver anonymity. Define a sender/receiver anonymity _**(1-p)**_ where _**p **_is the probability that an adversary watching the inputs/outputs of the bridge can link a single sender and receiver successfully as the time _**t -> infinity**_. Thus we want _**p -> 0 **_as _**t -> infinity**_.

Some initial ideas:
- Consider a hash function _**H**_, field _**F**_, AND elliptic curve _**E**_. Sample either a random element from _**F**_ or curve point from _**E**_, call this _**x**_.
- Given the deposit amount _**r**_, compute the following hash _**H^r(x).**_
- Withdraw from the bridge by proving some knowledge of an intermediate hash _**H^(r')(x)**_ to withdraw a value _**r' = r_i + r_j + r_k**_ and prove all necessary claims over the original claim (there's probably a lot more to think through here).


I see a problem around this not being possible, mostly due to not being able to track half-claimed deposits. It would be hard to link hashes together to prove that a person isn't withdrawing more than they should be allowed to. Nonetheless, wanted to spark the discussion.

EDG Working Groups: A Primer
body:
In Edgeware, working groups function as mission-based development orgs that are composed of members who share interests, needs, and passions. Where an Ambassador team is largely formed to promote a network in a variety of ways, Working Groups are intended to solve issues specific to a community while also growing community. 

**This post will detail the existing working groups, and also describe why you might want to create one and how they can operate.**


**What is a working group?**
[**"**A **working group**, or **working party**, is a group of experts working together to achieve specified goals. The groups are domain-specific and focus on discussion or activity around a specific subject area. The term can sometimes refer to an interdisciplinary collaboration of researchers working on new activities that would be difficult to sustain under traditional funding mechanisms (e.g., federal agencies)."](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Working_group)

title: How move a validator to another server / hosts, without changing the keys
body:
Hi, 

We are going to say that you want to move the Edgeware Validator to a new server and for this to work without having to **rotate** or **insert** the **sessions keys** again, you can copy them from one server to another.

So as of this step you have two servers ready


In the server where the validator is running 
No need stop the validator. 
open:
```cd  ~/.local/share/edgeware/chains/edgeware/keystore ```
```ls```



There are 4 files here, they are the 4 session keys, you must copy them to the new server


In the new server / hosts install the EDG Soft and start the node how sentry, no how validator.
so,
From the new server from where you have the keystore folder empty, the software is installed and the chain is sync the last block, run

```rsync -havz -e "ssh -p 2222" server@IP:/home/user/.local/share/edgeware/chains/edgeware/keystore $HOME/.local/share/edgeware/chains/edgeware/keystore```

here "ssh -p 2222"  **2222** change for your ssh port.

Now the 4 keys will be on your new server.

check here now the folder is not empty anymore
cd  ~/.local/share/edgeware/chains/edgeware/keystore


If oke, stop the other server where is running the validator and start the new one as validator, not as sentry.

> **Note:** *You can double sign and suffer slashed if you turn on both at the same time as validators with the keys. be careful.*

title: Commonwealth's Community Validator Program
body:
On the last community call, we discussed the importance of building an active validator ecosystem. We're excited to see the progress towards that goal — right now, 17% of EDG has already been staked, with the least nominated validator having ~10m EDG or 0.2% of the overall network staked towards them.

Today we’d like to announce Commonwealth's Community Validator Program. To build a larger active validator ecosystem, we’ll use Commonwealth’s genesis allocation to nominate smaller community validators to join the active set.

To participate, validators will need to fulfill some initial criteria:

1. Validate on Edgeware Berlin Testnet for a week without issues ([steps to get started on Github](https://github.com/hicommonwealth/edgeware-node) and on [docs.edgewa.re](https://docs.edgewa.re/understanding-edgeware/validating-on-edgeware-ui/validation/setting-up-a-node))
2. Create a [validator campaign here on Commonwealth](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/23-how-to-create-validator-councillor-campaigns).
3. Participate in our monthly Edgeware Community Call ([third Wednesday every month, at 2PM ET, link to calendar invite](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/r/eventedit/copy/YnQzMDFxNnFibGVoZ2Z0OHJ1cjVsbW03aGNfMjAyMDAyMTlUMTkwMDAwWiBjb21tb253ZWFsdGguaW1faWhiczg5MnBxdWJ2b2d0b2ltNmMxaGY3Y2tAZw/ZGlsbG9uY2hlbjEzQGdtYWlsLmNvbQ?scp=ALL&sf=true)).

title: Registrar Campaign: Thom Ivy, Commonwealth Labs
body:
## Proposal
I am proposing that Edgeware assign registrar status to my account, _kDyk...s1QF_ for the purpose of verifying the identities of Edgeware users via the judgement function. 

For an example of a verified ID, see below:

![](https://commonwealth-uploads.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/831c1727-613a-474e-9b41-7287571cc587.1582843293640)


## Problem
Currently, users have complained about not being able to /know/ from the Polkadot UI alone, that accounts claiming to be validators are who-they-say, a registrar can eliminate this issue by verifying that StakeStake 01, for instance, is truly under the control of the legal entity of StakeStake International. 

StakeStake would request a judgement on an ID from a registrar for a small fee, and prove that the account is not attempting to obtain nominations under pretense. 

While councils can alter IDs in Edgeware in cases of abuse, it would be better division of labor to use the Registrar system to maintain safe and clear ID records. For more on the registrar system, [click here.](https://wiki.polkadot.network/docs/en/learn-identity#registrars) 

## Solution
As a member of Edgeware's core development team, Commonwealth Labs, I am fully incentive aligned and possess the reputation to conduct registrar activities reliably. Assigning registrar status to me ensures at least one reputable agent can verify ID for validators and more. 

**This proposal is currently seeking seconds by EDG holders.**

title: Introducing Edgeware Working Groups
body:
## Join any of the Working Groups
[https://matrix.to/#/+edgeware-eco:matrix.org](https://matrix.to/#/+edgeware-eco:matrix.org)


**Intro**
To better organize the community for the first year of Edgeware, (and to launch a conversation on the refinement of these programs,) I’m introducing the Edgeware Working Group Assembly. While EDGWGA sounds more like a new screen size, instead it’s an evolution of the ambassador program we initially launched almost a year ago. That program had no mainnet to coalesce around at the time, but introduced several Edgeware fanatics and decentralized governance fans to each other - we invite them back now that the mainnet is launched.

Overall, it is my position that the traditional ambassador program common in cryptoeconomics is outdated- specifically for chains with on-chain governance enabled. Validators, formal governance leaders like Council members, tokenholders and developers now come together naturally to fulfill complementary ecosystem roles, laying the groundwork for collaboration that represents the diverse interests of these players. 

Finally, whereas ambassador programs had a barrier to entry, usually an application - the Edgeware Working Groups will be totally open to the public, enabling casual participants as well as the more intensive. I hope this brings even more diverse perspectives and involvement.

I will continue to be extremely active in organizing these groups and the broader community initiatives - but these groups will advance decentralization and democratic ownership of Edgeware significantly, and I believe it important to begin this work sooner rather than later, to avoid entrenched political or economic interests and hasten the rate of progress.

title: Tech Update #1: Finality, staking recommendations, and our first upgrade
body:
Hello Edgeware Community!

We're over 200,000 finalized blocks. The chain has been running fairly smoothly with some issues and we're working hard to address those, while continuing to push forward on product and interface improvements as well.

# Addressing finality issues

As it stands, the Edgeware node has been having some issues with validators not voting in the finalization process, leading finalization to stall and eventually triggering forced GRANDPA set updates. Not long ago with the help of [Andre Silva](https://github.com/andresilva) we merged in some changes to the GRANDPA service worker, and turned off forced finality changes to the Edgeware runtime. These changes will make their way into the first Edgeware runtime upgrade.

For technical details, please refer to:

1. [Disable GRANDPA finality fallback](https://github.com/hicommonwealth/edgeware-node/pull/141)
2. [Disable GRANDPA observer](https://github.com/hicommonwealth/edgeware-node/pull/140)

In addition to that, we've been actively following Substrate's work and the more stabler `polkadot-master` branch to peg our Edgeware updates to. We currently have an active PR up that addresses the new changes. In this update which will be the first upgrade freeze, we are cleaning up the following issues:

1. Crashes in the v1.0.1 node due to inproper time arithmetic
2. Memory leaks in the Edgeware node

# Staking issues

As most people in the community know, Edgeware experienced a [slashing event](https://polkascan.io/pre/edgeware/event?module=staking&event=Slash&page=1) at block 126,200. A majority of Staking Facilities sentry nodes stalled and dropped from the network due to a "too many open files" issue. What causes this is usually an improper `ulimit` parameter. Though, we can speculate that the node is creating many temp files to cause such issues.

title: Reimbursment of slashed funds (Staking Facilities update thread)
body:
Hi everyone,

I am opening this thread in order to be as transparent as possible about the approach we at Staking Facilities want to pursue with regards to the the slashing event from February 25th, which was due to a bug-induced downtime.

We wrote a post mortem about what specifically has happened which you can find here:
[https://medium.com/@stakingfac/postmortem-2020-02-25-edgeware-validator-outage-645a728dbd2f](https://medium.com/@stakingfac/postmortem-2020-02-25-edgeware-validator-outage-645a728dbd2f)

## **A. Staking Facilities Validators:**
After we went back online, we quickly regained 10% of the validator slots, but decided to shut down 5 of our 10 validators because the bug has not been fixed yet. Once we regain confidence that Edgeware can be run reliably, we will reevaluate our decision.

## **B. Reimbursement of slashed funds:**
For the reimbursement of our nominators funds, we chose the following process:
1.) We will publish a list with the affected accounts and the associated number of slashed token.
2.) Two weeks after publishing the list, we will send out the reimbursements. This will give everyone the chance to review the list in order to avoid mistakes in the distribution.
3.) Once all tokens are refunded, we will inject a treasury spend proposal to refund our upfront reimbursement
We chose this process so that the outcome of the proposal and the reimbursement of our nominators funds can be separated. Should we get funds allocated by the treasury before reimbursing our nominators, people would need to trust Staking Facilities to redistribute the funds, because Substrate only allows to submit one address as a beneficiary. Reimbursing our nominators in advance allows us to avoid any trust related issues.

title: Zero-knowledge Working Group
body:
Hi everyone! I want to jumpstart some discussion about how we can build out more interesting zero-knowledge tools for Substrate based chains and especially Edgeware. These can likely be projects we push through and fund with the Treasury as well as other grants from the Web3 Foundation if they strike those folks as appealing.

## Overview
Edgeware and every other substrate chain benefits from being written in Rust and compiled down to WASM.  This allows us to utilise any `no_std` Rust libraries in the native runtime and build interesting applications with tools developed by people even outside the blockchain community.

## ZK Tools on Edgeware
For the past months, from last year on, I've been exploring zero-knowledge tools in Substrate runtimes. My journey started trying to integrate [bellman](https://github.com/matter-labs/bellman) and [sapling-crypto](https://github.com/matter-labs/sapling-crypto) into Substrate, which proved challenging, and eventually settled on integrating the [dalek-cryptography's](https://github.com/dalek-cryptography) tool suite. This tool suite benefits from being written in pure rust.

Some active areas the community here can push forward:
1. Rewrite bellman with `no_std` compatibility as well as the `BN256` curve that is commonly used in Ethereum.
2. Rewrite sapling-crypto with `no_std` compatbility (dependent on bellman) to allow us to deploy roll_ups that are nearly exact to those being built for the Ethereum ecosystem.

## anon (anonymous group constructions and actions)
I've been long interested in zero knowledge applications for voting and mixing coins like [Miximus](https://github.com/barryWhiteHat/miximus) and [Semaphore](https://github.com/appliedzkp/semaphore). My goal within our ecosystem is to bring similar tools to the Substrate ecosystem.

So far, I've been working on a project called [anon](https://github.com/hicommonwealth/anon) which enables group construction and anonymous attestation in the groups. There is one group con

title: Registrar Process and Verification Tiers [Registrar Index 0]
body:
I am modeling our first Registrar after Chevdor over at Kusama - thanks to him for drawing these up. They may be revised and high-level ID's will be re-scrutinized according to any new standards in order to maintain effective reputation for influential actors in Edgeware.


## Tiers and Qualifications

**"KnownGood" **- Only available for users willing to meet in person, provide their legal name with ID documentation, or via webcam with 2 pieces of corroborating ID. Onchain details must match these IDs. Basically KYC'd.

**"Reasonable" ** - Only accounts with at least one communication channel listed (email, riot, twitter, etc..) will be considered. Each communication channel will be verified independently using challenges. The Reasonable level is only granted to account passing all challenges for each of it's communication channels listed.

Beyond these two affirmative judgements, we also have:

- Unknown - The default value, no judgement made yet.
- FeePaid - The user has paid the fee and verification is in process. I will likely not assign this one until automation is possible, because it must be 'cleared' before granting a new judgement.
- OutOfDate - The Registrar is noting that the data used to be good - perhaps previously Reasonable status, but is no longer relevant.
- LowQuality - Imprecise or not useful, but can be updated to achieve better status.
- Erroneous- Incorrect data, failed challenges, may indicate malicious intent.





## Process

Basically:
1. User sets on-chain Identity
2. User requests Judgement from a specific Registrar and pays any applicable fees.
3. User contacts Registrar for Judgement
4. Interactions with Registrar verify ID
5. Registrar submits judgement.


See more detailed guidance and screenshots at [Edgeware Docs: Identity](https://docs.edgewa.re/understanding-edgeware/identity-module).

title: New: Tipping Module
body:
> A separate Treasury subsystem exists to allow for an agile "tipping" process, whereby a reward may be given _without first having a pre-determined stakeholder_ group come to consensus on how much should be paid.
> A group of Tippers is determined through the config Trait. After half of these have declared some amount that they believe a particular reported reason deserves, then a countdown period is entered where any remaining members can declare their tip amounts also. After the close of the countdown period, the median of all declared tips is paid to the reported beneficiary, along with any finders fee, in case of a public (and bonded) original report. [Subtrate Treasury Docs](https://substrate.dev/rustdocs/master/pallet_treasury/index.html)

_"without first having a pre-determined stakeholder" -- _This is at odds with what Jam explained, which is that a collective must first be formed (in the same way that the Council is an expression of a collective) which is achieved through an upgrade. If there was a way to call an extrinsic from an account to enter into a Tippers group, and that occurred in regular intervals (similar to



## Possible Applications

- Schedule Rounds of Edgeware Recognition for OSS contributions, exemplary community participation, technical support, discussion/research, or other acts of contributions.

title: Feature Change Discussion: Auto Payout to Lazy Payout or Simple Payout
body:
In Edgeware, staking rewards are paid automatically at the end of eras.  However, for scaling and block-time stability, Polkadot and Kusama have opted to make this a triggered event - by a transaction. Initially, Lazy Payouts required a staker to claim rewards themselves within an expiry window.  The newer design, Simple Payouts.

> 
> Polkadot and Kusama **make stakers claim their rewards for past eras by submitting a transaction**. This naturally leads to spreading out reward distribution, as people make transactions at disparate times, **rather than updating the accounts of all stakers in a single block. **Even if everyone submitted a reward claim at the same time, the fact that they are individual transactions would allow the block construction algorithm to process only a limited number per block and ensure that the network maintains a constant block time.** If all rewards were sent out in one block, this could cause serious issues with the stability of the network.[ Polkadot Wiki](https://wiki.polkadot.network/docs/en/learn-simple-payouts)**

> Simple payouts requires one transaction per validator per era to claim rewards. The reason Polkadot requires this is to avoid an attack where someone has several thousand accounts nominating a single validator. The major cost in reward distribution is mutating the accounts in storage, and Polkadot cannot pay out several thousand accounts in a single transaction. **[Polkadot Wiki](https://wiki.polkadot.network/docs/en/learn-simple-payouts) **

Currently, Kusama/Polkadot _also _have implemented a 64-nominator limit per Validator. 

Under Simple Payouts, ANYONE can send the payout transaction - triggering ALL of the validators nominators to be paid out.  Lazy Payouts requires each user to submit their own.  A value-add that validators might bring is to conduct these mass-payout transactions out of their own pocket on behalf of their nominators. Service enhancement. :)

title: Reducing the Ideal Staking Rate from 80% to 50%
body:
Recently community members have discussed reducing the Ideal Staking Rate, a chain parameter, from 80% to 50%. 

>  "This value should probably lie between 0.3 and 0.6, and we originally set it at \chi_{ideal}=0.546"
[Web3F Research](https://research.web3.foundation/en/latest/polkadot/Token%20Economics.html)

The consequences of adjusting this down are not totally clear- so I'm attaching two modeling tools I've worked up, to help us explore the option. Both have a parameter for the Ideal Staking Rate that can be modified.

These tools have not been fully vetted for mathematical accuracy, but they SHOULD -  a team with a specialty would be an amazing grant recipient to develop these models into more usable and verified tools.

After some playing around, one item of note is that both models display a lower reward rate for stakers if we shift the ideal staking rate down.  That makes sense to me - we are using strong incentives to get it up to 80 - and rewards are a way to do that. Drop the goal post, and you may not need as much incentive to reach it.

title: Edgeware Upgrade Process
body:
Edgeware is a Substrate-based blockchain. If you're not familiar with [Substrate](https://substrate.dev/), it is a modular 'build-your-own' blockchain layer built by Parity Technologies that enables Edgeware's forkless upgrades, WASM runtime, and other benefits.

Substate is also a cutting-edge and fast-paced development by its own right. As time goes on, the version of Substrate that Edgeware is based upon will change, and we will periodically need or want to incorporate these changes into Edgeware.

For the first technology upgrade to Edgeware, we are working to incorporate changes to both the Substrate and Edgeware-specific functions.

**Substrate Improvements**
Since the launch of Edgeware Mainnet in November, many enhancements to Substrate have occured, for example:

- Changes to the balances and system modules.
- Basically the migration here moved "accounts" from the balances module to the system module.
- Resource efficiencies over previous versions.

title: Migration Alternatives: 'The Hard Spoon'
body:
With Substrate experiencing big changes, many chains are starting to wonder how best to upgrade when  on-chain data stores need to be migrated to new locations to 'preserve the chain' of the chain with newer versions of Substrate. 

I posted recently on the upgrade path as explained by Drew,  but [Emiel of Polkascan](https://matrix.to/#/!dQIXacXSBDQsPsWEYR:matrix.org/$eZ_YspsT-n0Ww_gK4YW3kZCPSkMLIRMIB4ckzkEmPq4?via=matrix.org&via=matrix.parity.io) recently brought to our attention an alternative he called 'Hard Spooning':

> You could perhaps consider a chain reset through a ‘hard spoon’. You could get a new chain with a genesis state that reflects the state of the current chain at a given future block. This is how the Kulupu mainnet migrated yesterday after consent of its users. The main argument was removing the complex migration path. This approach solves all your problems elegantly.

In addition, it is an elegant way to release testnet or canary-nets with historical blocks. Drew mentioned that Edgeware has some trading volume and halting the chain to perform this 'hard spoon' might result in some confusion on exchanges.

User. Remz raised the point that those exchanges 'rely on finalization, which is sometimes lagging for hours already.'  He also feels that the concern is unwarranted: "chains often start and stop deposits and handle these events internally."

@nasamura:matrix.org mentioned that the Kulupu run of this technique went smoothly, but that "If it takes too long to build a workable runtime upgrade or begins to grow in complexity I would favour the path that Kulupu took."

The technical challenges and potential options for multiple Substrate-layer migrations continue to unfold.  :-]

title: Edgeware priorities
body:
We've got a sizeable treasury and I'd like to get some discussion going about how we can best allocate it to best support the long-term grown of Edgeware and the Polkadot ecosystem broadly. 

Here are the top 3 priorities currently as I see it:

**1) Smart contract support **
Edgeware first appealed to me early on because of the promise to support smart contracts. This is an important service for the Polkadot ecosystem that won't be supported natively by the Polkadot relay chain. I haven't heard much talk of this since launch - is this being worked on? Could an allocation from the treasury help get this done quicker?

**2) Ethereum bridge **
Another Edgeware initiative that appealed to me early on but has been quiet since launch is the Ethereum bridge. Obviously a lot of EDG holders are also ETH holders and if we can be the first to build a bridge between Ethereum and the Polkadot ecosystem, there is a lot of value there. Is there anyone working on this? I think this is an initiative that we should be committing treasury funds to. 

**2) Exchange support**
As one of the first substrate-based chains that allows users to utilize nominated proof-of-stake, it's in the interest of the community to broaden our community base by getting supported on exchanges. Some exchanges like Binance and Huobi charge a listing fee. It could make sense to pursue this to be the first substrate-based chain to get listed on a major exchange. This initiative is a distant third for me though.

What do others think? Where should we focus on allocating treasury funding to?

title: A governance participation dividend
body:
There are only ~100-200 accounts that have staked KSM towards electing a councillor, and ~50 accounts that have staked EDG. On the other hand, there are ~2400 nominators on Kusama, and ~1000 nominators on Edgeware. Also, people voting for councillor(s) right now are disproportionately large token holders.

This is a proposal to produce a fixed reward of 1-2% per year, to be distributed towards all EDG balances that have been staked towards at least one councillor or councillor candidate.

- For example, if I have 100,000 EDG in an account and have 50,000 EDG locked to vote for a councillor, I would receive this reward on the 50,000 EDG.
- The requirement is that you have to stake towards a legitimate councillor candidate, not that you have to vote for one of the existing councillors. So we might also increase the set of councillor candidates, to e.g. 13 councillors + 13 candidates.


Benefits:
- **Simplicity.** I've spoken with several other people about ways to incentivize governance participation, including awarding EDG to anyone who has voted on a referendum every month. This is the simplest solution by far.
- **Should not increase centralization. **Any governance reward has to be set-and-forget; otherwise the friction of interacting with governance for a 1-2% reward would be high enough that only whales have real incentive to claim the reward.
- **Minimal and predictable effect on token dilution.** The inflation rate is low enough that staking rewards will continue to remain the main source of inflation on the network.


Potential downsides:
- **Could incentivize less informed community members to participate in governance.** I don't think this is necessarily a bad thing; in fact, this change seems like it incentivizes known community members and those with a public reputation to become councillors. The purpose of Edgeware isn't to maintain a purist ideal of governance but to figure out how all the community participants and stakeholders can govern the network m

title: Bounty concept: Display thresholds for palletes/actions
body:
Right now, it's difficult to tell what the threshold for successful actions pertaining to council motions, democracy actions, etc. are -- you can submit actions, have them technically succeed according to their own parameters, but fail to execute as they fail the check on the chain's threshold requirements. 

Jam says that for an action: "You need to go to the runtime and check out what you want to do, so if it's a treasury proposal, there should be an approveOrigin in the runtime that you can ctrl+f" and that "every pallet declares its own origins, so unfortunately it's not uniform at all."

An interface tool that reads and displays these or as part of our communication of runtime parameters is a small project that might be worth a bounty.


To view the thresholds in the runtime:
[https://github.com/hicommonwealth/edgeware-node/blob/master/node/runtime/src/lib.rs](https://github.com/hicommonwealth/edgeware-node/blob/master/node/runtime/src/lib.rs)

> .Moncc is a completely novel approach to cloud deployments. On one hand you can think of it as a deployment tool which replaces Docker Compose, Terraform and Kubernetes. On the other hand, it is like a platform by itself because it comes with a dedicated hub (they call it the “Moncchub”) — a hub full of ready to use components and stacks that are prepared and configured by experts. It isn’t a wrapper around Kubernetes nor a managed service but rather a new generation orchestration platform which helped us combine ease of deployment and management without sacrificing our freedom to architect our own node management stack as we wanted to.

> With Moncc, everything starts with a simple YAML “template” which we deploy on a “cluster” (eventually multi cloud). We ended up developing a simple set of “templates” to deploy and manage Parity Substrate-based nodes. Today, we are happy to make them available to the community and demo our usage of them.

title: Guide: Launching a Working Group
body:
### Prior Reading
- [Working Groups: A Primer and a List of Existing Groups](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/702-edg-working-groups-a-primer)
- [Working Groups: Community Growth Strategy for Edgeware](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/742-working-groups-community-growth-strategy-for-edgeware)



**What Working Groups can be created?**
Many types of WG can be valuable:
- Regional groups that serve to promote and use Edgeware and improve problems within certain regions, Asia, Africa, and South America are all great places to open a WG.
- Specific technology applications, Privacy for instance.
- Identity or Community-based solution groups: Minorities, Social Justice, or others.
- Many others! Share ideas, none are bad.
- Partnership groups: Like the Decred x Edgeware WG.


### 
### To launch a Working Group:
- Post a concept to [Commonwealth.im/Edgeware](http://commonwealth.im/Edgeware) to share your idea. Your working Group Idea should include:
- **A mission**: What is your group trying to achieve, build or solve?
- **A vision**: What does the world look like if your group succeeds? Inspire your audience
- **A guide to recruiting:** Who is your ideal member set? Describe them. What skills, interests, connections or resources do they have? This will help your readers both self-identify as potential group members and help members recruit others. These members might not only be people but **organizations** you're looking to onboard or partner with. If you know specifics, share them. **Working groups reach a self-sustainable threshold of about 50-60 members with 7-12 core and very active participants. This is your goal!**
- **A link to a chat group** you've created for your WG. Right now, Edgeware uses both forums and chat rooms for each working group that helps it organize conversation from long-form content.
- You can ask for a Commonwealth #wg-YourWorkingGroup channel in your post, (see the sidebar here,) which is what Commonweal

title: Working Groups: Community Growth Strategy for Edgeware
body:
### Goal:
Make smart contract platforms like Edgeware popular, meme-like, utilized and valuable.

### Need:
A committed, robust and self-sustaining community of users/developers to use, develop, secure ,maintain and evangelize the platform.
### 
### Problem:
How do you onboard community members reliably, sustainably, such that their presence and efforts are also maximized individually but also as a cohort in order to jumpstart/ bootstrap the arrival of the sustainable robust community in the quickest time possible?

Unsolved challenges:
- How do people enter a flow of introduction to various working groups, in order to find their tribe?

### 
### Prior Art:
- Previously Ambassador programs sought to connect people with highly aligned values or stake in the game with each other, led by a CMO-type role whose task was to organize the activities of Ambassadors, track progress, onboard new ambassadors, and occasionally reward tasks. Ambassador programs are hype-d out, the benefits barely accrued, and tit-for-tat arrangements are legally odious.
- Reversely, organic and decentralized meme-based efforts are more successful in lifting token price, onboarding new speculators, and shillers. If the payoff in the form of token price doesn't hit, these meme-movements crumble and resentment builds. These users have loosely aligned values, namely economic conditions that don't ensure they will cooperate with each other past certain points.


### Solution:

**The Working Group Collective**
Fuse the approaches to create a decentralized set of working groups that are self-organizing but centrally bootstrapped by a community architect.

**Value-aligned at the top, Token-Value aligned at the bottom.**
The Working Group approach aligns people on values, but also produce material, norms and values that can be disseminated organically to a broader community of speculators, who can serve to distribute in turn to the broader web. It's important to have the energy and memes come reliably fro

title: Trusted vs Trustless ETH bridge
body:
Hey all,

Wanted to swing some ideas past the community and gauge our appetite short/long-term. Over the past few weeks I've been working on an [ETH light client implementation inside of a substrate runtime.](https://github.com/hicommonwealth/substrate-eth-light-client) The goal of this project is to setup a light client that developers can then use to build applications on top of. Similarly, I have also spent some time along with [@raymondz](/edgeware/account/mae7JWE1EEMLcno2ZSB8dahwPqVPEyh8zik6dgNpQTvvucq) looking into ChainBridge's trusted ethereum bridge. I have gone through the setup flow and integrated the runtime modules into our develop branch; however, I personally plan on removing it as I don't love the trusted bridge flow.

The work for the light client will lead to a bridge. The Edgeware on ETH perspective requires some more time and work if we desire a trustless implementation, but the ETH on Edgeware perspective will be possible once this project is completed.

This leads me to the question, is there more interest to deploy a trusted solution that works in both directions or a trustless one which potentially longer time to finish and deploy. The main bottleneck is not ETH on Edgeware, it's Edgeware on ETH.

title: Proposal: Halting the treasury reward
body:
With the latest upgrade, we now have the ability to use on-chain governance to set the treasury reward rate:
stakingReward.setTreasuryReward
We have over 460m EDG in the treasury, and the minting rate is:
5256000 blocks/year * 95 EDG/block * $0.0055/EDG
= $2.75m/year
The Commonwealth development grant was 50m EDG worth ~$500k at the time. I see the chain deploying up to about $500k/year **at maximum** towards development, and similarly maybe $500k/year towards BD, community, and partnerships (both estimates probably err on the high side).

We may also want to budget around $500k for one-time expenses like exchange listings, initial wallet integrations, etc.

If this analysis holds, our current treasury should be enough to cover the next 2+ years of community expenses. If EDG appreciates, then it will be enough for significantly more than that.

As such, it seems like we should advance this proposal now:

- Set the treasury reward inflation rate to 0. If the treasury continues to accumulate funds from staking inefficiencies, up to a couple % of the chain per year, this is enough to keep us close to a sustainable path indefinitely.


We also have the option to set the treasury reward inflation rate to 5-10% of where it is right now, e.g 7.5 EDG/block ($200k/year). But this seems strictly inferior as an option.

It seems like halting the treasury reward would be a change that other community members support, per [@luckyve](/edgeware/account/mYSJW56dUwhuKGWM1vafo6eYm9jRLr6aFF4TXma5ECwF7Eh)'s [thread](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/434-unfair-reward) from earlier this year.

A concern would be that after halting the treasury reward right now, it would be difficult to turn it on again later, but I tend to believe it wouldn't be a problem so long as the community seems it has been well spent.

cc [@dillchen](/edgeware/account/hwJpK8k6Q1KR8F87u5KHfBghRRit7p5UYWC1ubPDwsjdh6s) as I believe he has worked on a proposed budget - would be interesting to see
